title.zh: 卷三百七十 列傳第一百二十九 王友直 李寶 成閔 趙密 劉子羽 呂祉 胡世將 鄭剛中
title.en: Volume 370 Biographies 129: Wang Youzhi, Li Bao, Cheng Min, Zhao Mi, Liu Ziyu, Lu Zhi, Hu Shijiang, Zheng Gangzhong
title.raw: 卷三百七十 列傳第一百二十九 王友直 李寶 成閔 趙密 劉子羽 呂祉 胡世將 鄭剛中 Volume 370 Biographies 129: Wang Youzhi, Li Bao, Cheng Min, Zhao Mi, Liu Ziyu, Lu Zhi, Hu Shijiang, Zheng Gangzhong

sentences.zh: 王友直 李寶 成閔 趙密 劉子羽 呂祉 胡世將 鄭剛中

translations.literal: Wang Youzhi, Li Bao, Cheng Min, Zhao Mi, Liu Ziyu, Lu Zhi, Hu Shijiang, Zheng Gangzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhi, Li Bao, Cheng Min, Zhao Mi, Liu Ziyu, Lu Zhi, Hu Shijiang, and Zheng Gangzhong

sentences.zh: 王友直

translations.literal: Wang Youzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhi

sentences.zh: 王友直，字聖益，博州高平人。

translations.literal: Wang Youzhi, style name Shengyi, was a native of Gaoping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhi, whose style name was Shengyi, came from Gaoping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 父佐，以材武稱。

translations.literal: His father Zuo was renowned for talent and martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zuo was known for his ability and military skill.

sentences.zh: 友直年十二，隨父游，諳兵法。

translations.literal: At age twelve Youzhi accompanied his father on his travels and became versed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve, Youzhi traveled with his father and learned the art of war.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，金人渝盟，友直結豪傑，志恢復。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Shaoxing the Jin violated the treaty; Youzhi rallied bold spirits with the aim of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, when the Jin broke the peace treaty, Youzhi gathered local heroes determined to recover the lost north.

sentences.zh: 謂其眾曰：「權所以濟事，權歸於正，何害於理。」

translations.literal: He said to his followers: "Expedient measures exist to accomplish affairs; when expedients return to what is right, what harm is there to principle?"
translations.idiomatic: He told his followers, "Expedients exist to get things done; once an expedient serves the right cause, principle is not harmed."

sentences.zh: 乃矯制自擬承宣使、河北等路安撫制置使，餘擬官有差，遍諭州縣勤王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he forged an edict and appointed himself Commissioner for the Propagation of Edicts and Pacification and Reorganization Commissioner for Hebei and other circuits, with other provisional offices at various ranks, and sent orders throughout prefectures and counties to rally to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He then forged an imperial commission, naming himself Commissioner for the Propagation of Edicts and Pacification and Reorganization Commissioner for Hebei and other circuits, filled other offices as needed, and called on every prefecture and county to rise for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，得眾數萬，制為十三軍，軍置都統制、提舉、提點、提轄、訓練統之。

translations.literal: Before long he mustered tens of thousands of men, organized them into thirteen armies, and in each army established a commander-in-chief, an intendant, an inspector, a controller, and a trainer to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he had tens of thousands of followers, which he organized into thirteen armies, each with its own commander-in-chief, intendant, inspector, controller, and trainer.

sentences.zh: 九月戊子，進攻大名，一鼓而克，撫定眾庶，諭以紹興年號。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi of the ninth month he attacked Daming, took it at the first assault, pacified the populace, and proclaimed the Shaoxing reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the ninth month he attacked Daming, captured it in a single assault, reassured the people, and announced the Shaoxing reign era.

sentences.zh: 乃與王任、馮谷、張升、牛汝霖列奏於朝，欲領眾南歸。

translations.literal: He then jointly memorialized the court with Wang Ren, Feng Gu, Zhang Sheng, and Niu Rulin, wishing to lead his forces south in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Wang Ren, Feng Gu, Zhang Sheng, and Niu Rulin in a joint memorial to the court, asking to bring their forces south.

sentences.zh: 時金人尚在揚州，久不報。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin were still at Yangzhou, and for a long time there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army was still at Yangzhou, and the court did not answer for a long time.

sentences.zh: 友直將由壽春涉淮而濟，道拜敕書勉以率眾搗敵腹心，掎角應援。

translations.literal: Youzhi was about to cross the Huai from Shouchun when along the way he received an edict urging him to lead his forces to strike the enemy's vitals and coordinate supporting attacks from another angle.
translations.idiomatic: As Youzhi was preparing to cross the Huai from Shouchun, he received an imperial edict en route urging him to lead his men against the enemy's heartland and coordinate supporting strikes.

sentences.zh: 除友直檢校少保、天雄軍節度使，王任天平軍節度使，馮谷左通議大夫、徽猷閣直學士，張升右朝奉大夫、直秘閣，牛汝霖通直郎、直秘閣，職任各從舊，得便宜行事。

translations.literal: Youzhi was appointed Acting Junior Guardian, Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army; Wang Ren Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Feng Gu Left Grand Master for Discussion and Academician Expositor of the Huixian Pavilion; Zhang Sheng Right Grand Master for Court Service and Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion; Niu Rulin Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance and Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion; each retained his former duties and was authorized to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was made Acting Junior Guardian and Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army; Wang Ren Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Feng Gu Left Grand Master for Discussion and Academician Expositor of the Huixian Pavilion; Zhang Sheng Right Grand Master for Court Service and Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion; and Niu Rulin Gentleman for Direct Remonstrance and Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion. Each kept his former responsibilities and was granted discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 時三十二年正月一日也。

translations.literal: This was on the first day of the first month of the thirty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: This took place on the first day of the first month of 1162.

sentences.zh: 旋與敵遇，相拒淮北；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he encountered the enemy and faced them north of the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he met the enemy and held them north of the Huai;

sentences.zh: 敵兵來益眾，友直即率所部渡淮。

translations.literal: as enemy troops grew ever more numerous, Youzhi at once led his command across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: but as Jin forces kept growing, Youzhi led his troops across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 既而審金主亮已斃，所遇乃歸師，悔不襲擊之。

translations.literal: He then learned that the Jin ruler Liang had already died and that the force he had met was a returning army; he regretted not having attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: He then learned that the Jin emperor Wanyan Liang was already dead and that the troops he had faced were a retreating column; he regretted not having struck them.

sentences.zh: 高宗視師江上，見於金陵，賜金帶、章服，錫賚及二子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong inspected the army on the Yangtze and received him at Jinling, bestowing a gold belt, official robes, gifts, and rewards on his two sons as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong inspected the army on the Yangtze, he received Youzhi at Jinling and granted him a gold belt, court robes, gifts, and rewards for his two sons.

sentences.zh: 友直恥前功不遂，自陳，改復州防禦使，以忠義軍統制隸鎮江都統司。

translations.literal: Ashamed that his earlier achievements had not been fulfilled, Youzhi presented himself and was reassigned Defender of Fuzhou, with command of the Loyal and Righteous Army under the Jiangdu Commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his earlier campaign had not fully succeeded, Youzhi petitioned the throne and was reassigned Defender of Fuzhou, commanding the Loyal and Righteous Army under the Jiangdu headquarters.

sentences.zh: 越四月，詔偕統制張子蓋援海州。

translations.literal: Four months later he was ordered to join Commander Zhang Zigai in relieving Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four months later he was ordered to join Commander Zhang Zigai in relieving Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 方接戰，友直張一旗，大書「宋忠義將河北王九郎」以自表。

translations.literal: As battle was joined, Youzhi raised a banner boldly inscribed "Song Loyal and Righteous General Wang the Ninth Son of Hebei" to declare himself.
translations.idiomatic: As the battle opened, Youzhi raised a banner reading "Song Loyal and Righteous General Wang the Ninth Son of Hebei" to announce himself.

sentences.zh: 潛由小逕背敵陣，因其輜重，扼歸道橋，左右枕水。

translations.literal: He secretly took a narrow path behind the enemy line, seized upon their baggage train, blocked the bridge on their line of retreat, with water on both flanks.
translations.idiomatic: He stole along a side path behind the enemy, seized their baggage train, and blocked the bridge on their retreat route, with water on both sides.

sentences.zh: 張子蓋知友直已乘敵後，麾軍進擊，敵潰走，盡溺死，圍遂解。

translations.literal: Zhang Zigai, knowing Youzhi had already taken the enemy's rear, commanded the army forward; the enemy broke and fled, all drowning, and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zigai saw that Youzhi had taken the enemy's rear, he ordered a frontal assault; the enemy broke and fled, drowning in great numbers, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 轉宜州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Observer of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Observer of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，友直與統制宋寧數出奇轉戰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, Youzhi and Commander Song Ning repeatedly launched surprise attacks in shifting battles.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Youzhi and Commander Song Ning won repeated victories with daring maneuvers.

sentences.zh: 張浚都督江、淮，一見喜之，辟建康前軍統制。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was supreme commander on the Yangtze and Huai; at first sight he took a liking to him and appointed him Commander of the Vanguard Army at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, supreme commander on the Yangtze and Huai, took an immediate liking to him and appointed him commander of the Jiankang vanguard.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年九月，金人犯邊，宣諭使王之望命以前軍戍昭關，友直不逾時即行。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Longxing the Jin invaded the frontier; Commissioner Wang Zhiwang ordered the vanguard to garrison Zhaoguan, and Youzhi set out without delay.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1164, when the Jin invaded the border, Commissioner Wang Zhiwang ordered the vanguard to hold Zhaoguan, and Youzhi marched at once.

sentences.zh: 他軍同戍者，敵至，輒退保和州，友直孤軍堅守。

translations.literal: Other armies garrisoned there, when the enemy arrived, at once withdrew to defend Hezhou; Youzhi alone held fast with an isolated force.
translations.idiomatic: Other units stationed with him retreated to Hezhou as soon as the enemy appeared, but Youzhi held his isolated post.

sentences.zh: 金兵駐黃山，鼓柝相聞，益整暇自持。

translations.literal: The Jin army encamped at Huangshan; drums and night watches could be heard from one another, yet he grew all the more composed and self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin encamped at Huangshan within earshot of his drums and watches, yet he remained calm and resolute.

sentences.zh: 李寶，河北人。

translations.literal: Li Bao was a man of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao was from Hebei.

sentences.zh: 嘗陷金，拔身從海道來歸。

translations.literal: He had once fallen into Jin hands but escaped and returned by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been captured by the Jin but escaped and made his way back by sea.

sentences.zh: 金主亮渝盟，淮、浙奸民倪詢、梁簡等教金造舟，且為鄉導。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Liang violated the treaty, treacherous natives of Huai and Zhe such as Ni Xun and Liang Jian taught the Jin to build ships and also served as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor Wanyan Liang broke the treaty, local collaborators in Huai and Zhe such as Ni Xun and Liang Jian taught the Jin to build ships and guided them.

sentences.zh: 金使蘇保衡造舟於潞河。

translations.literal: The Jin dispatched Su Baoheng to build ships on the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Su Baoheng to build ships on the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 明年，以保衡為統軍，將繇海道襲浙江。

translations.literal: The next year Su Baoheng was made commander-in-chief and was to strike Zhejiang by sea.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Su Baoheng was made commander-in-chief and was to attack Zhejiang by sea.

sentences.zh: 諜聞，高宗謂宰臣曰：「李寶頃因召對，詢以北事，歷歷如數。

translations.literal: When spies reported this, Emperor Gaozong said to his chief ministers: "When Li Bao was recently summoned for audience and questioned about northern affairs, he answered item by item as if counting them off.
translations.idiomatic: When intelligence reached the court, Emperor Gaozong told his chief ministers, "When Li Bao was recently summoned, he answered every question about the north as if he had counted them out.

sentences.zh: 且以一介脫身還朝，陛對無一毫沮懾，是必能事者。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as a lone man he escaped and returned to court; in audience before the throne he showed not the slightest dismay—he is surely one who can accomplish affairs."
translations.idiomatic: And he escaped alone to return to court, showing not a trace of fear in audience—he is clearly a man who can get things done."

sentences.zh: 乃授浙西路馬步軍副總管，駐劄平江，令與守臣督海舟捍禦。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Deputy Commander of the Zhexi Circuit Horse and Foot Army, stationed at Pingjiang, and ordered with the defending officials to supervise sea vessels for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed Deputy Commander of the Zhexi Circuit Horse and Foot Army, stationed at Pingjiang, and ordered to work with local officials in preparing coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 高宗問：「舟幾何？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong asked: "How many vessels?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How many ships do you have?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「堅全可涉風濤者，百二十艘。」

translations.literal: He replied: "One hundred and twenty that are sound and able to brave wind and waves."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "One hundred and twenty sturdy enough to face wind and waves."

sentences.zh: 「兵幾何？」

translations.literal: How many troops?"
translations.idiomatic: And how many men?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「僅三千，皆閩、浙弓弩手，非正兵也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Only three thousand, all archers and crossbowmen from Min and Zhe—not regular troops.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Only three thousand, all archers and crossbowmen from Fujian and Zhejiang—not regular troops.

sentences.zh: 旗幟甲仗亦粗備。

translations.literal: Banners, flags, and armor and weapons are also roughly in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Banners, armor, and weapons are also roughly in order.

sentences.zh: 事急矣，臣願亟發。」

translations.literal: The matter is urgent; your servant wishes to set out at once."
translations.idiomatic: The situation is urgent, and I beg to sail at once."

sentences.zh: 賜寶衣帶、鞍馬、尚方弓刀、戈甲及銀絹萬數。

translations.literal: He was granted precious robes and belt, saddle horse, imperial bows and blades, spears and armor, and tens of thousands in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him court robes and belt, saddle horse, imperial bows and blades, spears and armor, and large sums in silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 八月，次江陰，先遣其子公佐，謂曰：「汝為潛伺敵動靜虛實，毋誤。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month he halted at Jiangyin and first sent his son Gongzuo, saying to him: "You are to spy out the enemy's movements and strength in secret—do not fail."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he halted at Jiangyin and first sent his son Gongzuo, telling him, "Go spy out the enemy's movements and strength in secret—do not fail."

sentences.zh: 公佐受命，即與將官邊士甯偕往。

translations.literal: Gongzuo received the order and at once went with the officer Bian Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzuo accepted the mission and set out at once with the officer Bian Shining.

sentences.zh: 寶將啟行，軍士爭言西北風力尚勁，迎之非利。

translations.literal: As Bao was about to set sail, the soldiers all argued that the northwest wind was still strong and that sailing into it would be disadvantageous.
translations.idiomatic: As Bao was about to sail, his men protested that the northwest wind was still strong and that sailing into it would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 寶下令，敢沮大計者斬。

translations.literal: Bao issued an order: whoever dared obstruct the grand plan would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Bao ordered that anyone who obstructed the plan would be executed.

sentences.zh: 遂發蘇州，大洋行三日，風甚惡，舟散不可收。

translations.literal: He then sailed from Suzhou; on the open sea after three days the wind grew very fierce and the vessels scattered beyond recall.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed from Suzhou; after three days on the open sea a violent storm scattered the fleet beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 寶忼慨顧左右曰：「天以是試李寶邪？

translations.literal: Bao, indignant, looked about him and said: "Is Heaven testing Li Bao with this?
translations.idiomatic: Bao looked around his men and said bitterly, "Is Heaven testing Li Bao?

sentences.zh: 寶心如鐵石，不變矣。」

translations.literal: Li Bao's heart is like iron and stone and will not change."
translations.idiomatic: My heart is iron and will not change."

sentences.zh: 酹酒自誓，風即止。

translations.literal: He poured a libation and swore an oath to himself, and the wind at once ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He poured a libation and swore his resolve, and the wind died down.

sentences.zh: 明日，散舟復集。

translations.literal: The next day the scattered vessels gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the scattered ships reassembled.

sentences.zh: 士寧自密州回，得敵耗甚悉，且言公佐已挾魏勝得海州。

translations.literal: Shining returned from Mizhou with very detailed intelligence on the enemy, and also reported that Gongzuo, with Wei Sheng's help, had already taken Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Shining returned from Mizhou with detailed intelligence and reported that Gongzuo, with Wei Sheng's help, had already taken Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 寶喜曰：「吾兒不負乃翁矣。」

translations.literal: Bao said in delight: "My son has not failed his old father."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said with delight, "My son has not failed his father."

sentences.zh: 士氣百倍，趣眾乘機進。

translations.literal: Morale increased a hundredfold, and he urged the army to advance and seize the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Morale soared, and he pressed his men to advance while the moment was ripe.

sentences.zh: 適大風復作，海濤如山，寶神色不為動；

translations.literal: Just then a great wind rose again and sea waves were like mountains, yet Bao's expression did not change;
translations.idiomatic: Just then another great storm arose and the waves rose like mountains, but Bao's expression did not change;

sentences.zh: 風少殺，始縱舟泊抵東海。

translations.literal: when the wind abated somewhat he at last let the vessels sail and anchored off the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: when the wind eased he sailed on and anchored off the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 敵已雲合，圍海州，旌麾數十里。

translations.literal: The enemy had already massed like clouds, besieging Haizhou, their banners and flags stretching for tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already massed in clouds around Haizhou, their banners stretching for miles.

sentences.zh: 寶麾兵登岸，以劍畫地，令曰：「此非復吾境，力戰與否在汝等。」

translations.literal: Bao commanded the troops ashore, drew a line on the ground with his sword, and ordered: "This is no longer our territory; whether you fight with all your strength is up to you."
translations.idiomatic: Bao led his men ashore, drew a line in the ground with his sword, and said, "This is no longer our land—whether you fight with all your might is up to you."

sentences.zh: 因握槊前行，遇敵奮擊，將士賈勇，無不一當十。

translations.literal: He then grasped his spear and advanced; meeting the enemy he struck fiercely, and officers and soldiers summoned their courage, each fighting as ten.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his spear and charged forward; officers and men fought with such fury that each seemed worth ten.

sentences.zh: 敵出不意，亟引去。

translations.literal: The enemy, caught unawares, at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Caught by surprise, the enemy withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 勝出城迎，寶獎其忠義，勉以共立功名，勝感泣。

translations.literal: Sheng came out of the city to welcome him; Bao praised his loyalty and righteousness and urged him to share in establishing merit and fame; Sheng wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng came out to welcome him; Bao praised his loyalty and urged him to share in winning glory together, and Sheng wept.

sentences.zh: 乃維舟犒士，遺辯者四出招納降附，聲振山東。

translations.literal: He then moored the vessels and rewarded the troops, sent four eloquent envoys in all directions to recruit surrenders and adherents, and his fame shook Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He anchored to reward his men and sent four eloquent envoys in all directions to rally defectors; his fame resounded across Shandong.

sentences.zh: 豪傑如王世修輩各署旗，集義勇，爭應援，多者數萬人。

translations.literal: Bold spirits such as Wang Shixiu each raised their own banners, gathered righteous volunteers, and vied to answer his call; some mustered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Local heroes such as Wang Shixiu raised their own banners, gathered volunteers, and rushed to join him—some with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 寶列名上諸朝，檄所部會密之膠西，命公佐以郡事畀勝，與俱發。

translations.literal: Bao submitted lists of names to the court, ordered his command to assemble at Jiaoxi in Mizhou, entrusted the prefectural affairs to Sheng through Gongzuo, and set out together.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent lists of names to the court, ordered his forces to assemble at Jiaoxi in Mizhou, left the prefecture to Gongzuo and Wei Sheng, and marched with them.

sentences.zh: 至膠西石臼島，敵舟已出海口，泊唐島，相距僅一山。

translations.literal: When they reached Shijiu Island off Jiaoxi, the enemy vessels had already left the harbor mouth and anchored at Tang Island, separated by only one mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Shijiu Island off Jiaoxi they found the enemy fleet already out of the harbor and anchored at Tang Island, only a mountain apart.

sentences.zh: 時北風盛，寶禱于石臼神。

translations.literal: At that time the north wind was strong; Bao prayed to the god of Shijiu.
translations.idiomatic: The north wind was strong, and Bao prayed to the god of Shijiu.

sentences.zh: 俄有風自柂樓中來，如鐘鐸聲，眾鹹奮，引舟握刃待戰。

translations.literal: Shortly a wind came from the stern castle like the sound of bells and clappers; all were stirred, drew up the vessels, grasped their blades, and awaited battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a wind rose from the stern like the sound of bells; the men took heart, drew up their ships, gripped their weapons, and waited to fight.

sentences.zh: 敵操舟者皆中原遺民，遙見寶船，紿敵兵入舟中，使不知王師猝至。

translations.literal: The enemy sailors were all former subjects of the Central Plains; seeing Bao's ships from afar, they deceived the enemy troops into boarding the vessels so they would not know the imperial army had arrived suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sailors were all former subjects of the Central Plains; seeing Bao's ships from afar, they lured the Jin troops aboard so they would not know the Song fleet had arrived.

sentences.zh: 風駛舟疾，過山薄虜，鼓聲震疊，海波騰躍。

translations.literal: The wind drove the vessels swiftly; passing the mountain they closed on the barbarians; drums thundered in layers and sea waves leaped.
translations.idiomatic: The wind drove them swiftly past the mountain toward the enemy; drums thundered and the sea churned.

sentences.zh: 敵大驚，掣矴舉帆，帆皆油纈，彌亙數里，風浪卷聚一隅，窘束無復行次。

translations.literal: The enemy were greatly alarmed, hauled up anchors and raised sails—all sails were oiled and varnished, stretching for miles; wind and waves swept them into one corner, cramped and unable to maintain formation.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked, raised anchor and set sail—their oiled sails stretched for miles—but wind and waves swept them into a corner where they could no longer maneuver.

sentences.zh: 寶亟命火箭環射，箭所中，煙焰旋起，延燒數百艘。

translations.literal: Bao at once ordered fire-arrows shot all around; wherever arrows struck, smoke and flame rose at once, spreading to burn hundreds of vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Bao ordered fire-arrows shot in all directions; wherever they struck, flames rose and spread to hundreds of ships.

sentences.zh: 火所不及者猶欲前拒，寶叱壯士躍登其舟，短兵擊刺，殪之舟中。

translations.literal: Those the fire had not reached still wished to advance and resist; Bao shouted for stalwarts to leap aboard their vessels, strike with close weapons, and slay them in the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ships untouched by fire still tried to resist; Bao ordered his strongest men to board and kill the enemy in hand-to-hand fighting on deck.

sentences.zh: 余所謂簽軍，盡中原舊民，皆登島垠，脫甲歸命，以故不殺。

translations.literal: The so-called tally troops were all former Central Plains people; they all came ashore on the island bank, cast off armor, and submitted—therefore they were not killed.
translations.idiomatic: The tally troops were all former Central Plains subjects; they came ashore, cast off their armor, and surrendered, and so were spared.

sentences.zh: 然倉卒，舟不獲艤，溺死甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet in the haste vessels could not be moored, and very many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: But in the confusion many ships could not be secured, and a great number drowned.

sentences.zh: 俘大漢軍三千餘人，斬其帥完顏鄭家奴等六人，禽倪詢等上於朝，獲其統軍符印與文書、器甲、糧斛以萬計。

translations.literal: More than three thousand Great Han troops were captured; six of their commanders including Wanyan Zhengjianu were beheaded; Ni Xun and others were seized and sent up to court; command seals, documents, weapons, armor, and grain in the tens of thousands were taken.
translations.idiomatic: They captured more than three thousand Han troops, beheaded six enemy commanders including Wanyan Zhengjianu, sent Ni Xun and other collaborators to court, and seized command seals, documents, weapons, armor, and grain by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 餘物眾不能舉者，悉焚之，火四晝夜不滅。

translations.literal: Remaining goods the multitude could not carry away were all burned; the fire did not die for four days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: What they could not carry away they burned; the fire burned for four days and nights.

sentences.zh: 寶將乘勢席捲，公佐切諫，以為金主亮方濟淮，聞通、泰已陷，得遠失近，且有腹背憂。

translations.literal: Bao wished to sweep forward with the momentum, but Gongzuo urgently remonstrated, holding that the Jin ruler Liang was just crossing the Huai, and hearing that Tong and Tai had fallen he would gain the distant and lose the near, and moreover face danger front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wanted to press the advantage, but Gongzuo urgently advised that Wanyan Liang was crossing the Huai and, hearing that Tongzhou and Taizhou had fallen, would face enemies both ahead and behind.

sentences.zh: 乃還軍駐東海，視緩急為表裏援。

translations.literal: He therefore returned the army to garrison the Eastern Sea, watching urgency and ease to serve as inner and outer support.
translations.idiomatic: Bao therefore withdrew to the Eastern Sea and stood ready to support the main front as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 遣曹洋輕舟報捷。

translations.literal: He sent Cao Yang in a light vessel to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cao Yang in a fast boat to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「朕獨用李寶，果立功，為天下倡矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in delight: "I alone employed Li Bao, and he has indeed achieved merit—he will be the model for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, "I trusted Li Bao alone, and he has indeed won a great victory—he will be the model for the whole realm."

sentences.zh: 詔獎諭，書「忠勇李寶」四字，表其旗幟。

translations.literal: An edict commended and instructed him, inscribing the four characters "Loyal and Valiant Li Bao" to adorn his banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and inscribed the four characters "Loyal and Valiant Li Bao" on his banners.

sentences.zh: 除靜海軍節度使、沿海制置使，賜金器、玉帶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army and Coastal Reorganization Commissioner, and granted gold vessels and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of the Jinghai Army and Coastal Reorganization Commissioner, and granted gold vessels and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 亮聞膠西之敗，大怒，召諸酋約以三日渡江，於是內變殺亮。

translations.literal: Liang, hearing of the defeat at Jiaoxi, was greatly enraged, summoned the chieftains and pledged to cross the Yangtze within three days; thereupon an internal mutiny killed Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Liang heard of the defeat at Jiaoxi, he flew into a rage, summoned his chiefs, and vowed to cross the Yangtze within three days; an internal mutiny then killed him.

sentences.zh: 向微唐島之捷，則亮之死未可期，錢唐之危可憂也。

translations.literal: Had there not been the victory at Tang Island, Liang's death could not have been foreseen and the peril to Qiantang would have been worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: Without the victory at Tang Island, Liang's death might never have come and Qiantang would have been in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 寶之功亦大矣。

translations.literal: Bao's achievement was also great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao's achievement was truly great.

sentences.zh: 寶戰具精利，宰臣陳康伯取其長槍、克敵弓弩，俾所司為式制之。

translations.literal: Bao's weapons were refined and sharp; Chief Minister Chen Kangbo took his long spears and enemy-defeating crossbows and had the relevant offices make them according to model patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's weapons were exceptionally fine; Chief Minister Chen Kangbo ordered his long spears and enemy-defeating crossbows to be copied as standard issue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈檢校少保。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Acting Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Acting Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 成閔，字居仁，邢州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Min, style name Juren, was a native of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Min, whose style name was Juren, came from Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，劉韐為真定帥，募勇士捍金兵，閔在麾下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang Liu Ge was commander at Zhending and recruited bold warriors to resist the Jin army; Min was in his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era Liu Ge was commander at Zhending and recruited warriors to resist the Jin; Min served under him.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，閔領數百騎至揚州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Min led several hundred horsemen to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Min led several hundred horsemen to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會上南渡，韓世忠追苗傅及襲兀術、討範汝為，閔皆在戎行，又以力戰卻敵，積功至武功大夫、忠州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor crossed south, in Han Shizhong's pursuit of Miao Fu, assault on Wuzhu, and campaign against Fan Ruwei, Min was always in the ranks; moreover through fierce fighting he repelled the enemy and accumulated merit until he reached Grand Master of Martial Achievement and Prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled south, Min fought in Han Shizhong's campaigns against Miao Fu, Wuzhu, and Fan Ruwei, and through repeated fierce combat rose to Grand Master of Martial Achievement and Prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從世忠入見，世忠指閔曰：「臣在南京，自謂天下當先，使當時見此人，亦避一頭矣。」

translations.literal: Accompanying Shizhong to audience, Shizhong pointed to Min and said: "When your servant was at Nanjing I considered myself foremost in the realm; had I met this man then, I too would have yielded a place."
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied Shizhong to court, Shizhong pointed to him and said, "At Nanjing I thought myself the foremost fighter in the realm; had I met this man then, I would have stepped aside."

sentences.zh: 上嘉歎勞勉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed, commending and encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and encouraged him warmly.

sentences.zh: 旋以取海州功，擢磁州團練使。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for the merit of taking Haizhou, he was promoted to Militia Training Commissioner of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for capturing Haizhou, he was promoted to Militia Training Commissioner of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜袍帶、錦帛，加贈玉束帶。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, he was granted robes and belt, brocade and silk, and additionally given a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience he was granted robes, belt, brocade and silk, and a jade belt as well.

sentences.zh: 時方與金盟，世忠罷兵，入為樞密使，詔進閔棣州防禦使、殿前游奕軍統制，曆遷保甯軍承宣使。

translations.literal: At that time a treaty had just been made with the Jin; Shizhong dismissed his troops and entered office as Vice Minister of the Secretariat; an edict advanced Min to Defender of Dizhou and Commander of the Palace Roaming Patrol Army, and he was successively transferred to Commissioner of the Baoning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had just been made with the Jin; Shizhong disbanded his army and became Vice Minister of the Secretariat; Min was promoted to Defender of Dizhou and Commander of the Palace Roaming Patrol Army, and later to Commissioner of the Baoning Army.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年，拜慶遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1154 he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，詔起復，贈其母鄭國夫人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he mourned his mother; an edict recalled him from mourning; his mother was posthumously granted the title Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; the court recalled him from mourning and posthumously granted his mother the title Lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 金主亮將敗盟，詔閔提禁旅三萬鎮武昌，命湖北守、漕創砦屋三萬間以待之，發折帛米錢茶引共百四十余萬緡、義倉和糶米六十三萬石備軍用，仍賜金器、劍甲臨遣之。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Liang was about to break the treaty, Min was ordered to lead thirty thousand imperial guards to garrison Wuchang; Hubei prefects and transport commissioners were ordered to build thirty thousand barrack rooms in readiness; folded-cloth money, rice money, and tea certificates totaling more than 1.4 million strings, and 630,000 shi of charity-granary and relief grain were issued for military use; gold vessels, swords, and armor were also granted on his departure.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Liang was about to break the treaty, Min was ordered to lead thirty thousand imperial guards to Wuchang; Hubei officials were told to build thirty thousand barracks, and more than 1.4 million strings in cash equivalents plus 630,000 shi of grain were set aside for the army; he was also sent off with gold vessels, swords, and armor.

sentences.zh: 閔至鄂，未幾，進屯應城縣。

translations.literal: Min reached Ezhou and before long advanced to encamp at Yingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Min reached Ezhou and soon advanced to camp at Yingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 八月，除湖北、京西制置使，節制兩路軍馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed Reorganization Commissioner for Hubei and Jingxi and given command over the armies of both circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made Reorganization Commissioner for Hubei and Jingxi with command over both circuits' armies.

sentences.zh: 九月，兼京西、河北招討使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was additionally made Pacification Commissioner for Jingxi and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was also made Pacification Commissioner for Jingxi and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔回援淮西。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was ordered to return and relieve Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was ordered back to reinforce Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 閔喜於得歸，冒雨兼程趨建康，士卒多道死，朝廷所給犒師物奄歸己，不及士卒。

translations.literal: Delighted at returning, Min rushed through rain day and night toward Jiankang; many soldiers died on the road; the rewards the court had given to comfort the army he kept entirely for himself and did not pass them to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Glad to be heading home, Min rushed through rain day and night toward Jiankang; many soldiers died on the march; he kept the court's reward goods for himself and gave nothing to the men.

sentences.zh: 士卒有怨言，閔斬之。

translations.literal: When soldiers murmured in complaint, Min beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: When the men complained, he had them executed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除淮東制置使，駐鎮江。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Reorganization Commissioner for Huaidong and stationed at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Reorganization Commissioner for Huaidong and stationed at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 既而言者論諸軍皆聚鎮江，恐敵出不意搗上流，於是詔閔發鄂州張成、華旺軍回駐鄂。

translations.literal: Thereafter critics argued that concentrating all armies at Zhenjiang might allow the enemy to strike unexpectedly upriver; an edict then ordered Min to send Zhang Cheng's and Hua Wang's armies from Ezhou back to garrison E.
translations.idiomatic: Critics then warned that massing every army at Zhenjiang left the upper Yangtze exposed; the court ordered Min to send Zhang Cheng's and Hua Wang's forces from Ezhou back to E.

sentences.zh: 亮死，閔引兵渡江趨揚州。

translations.literal: When Liang died, Min led his troops across the river toward Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang's death, Min crossed the river toward Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及金人自盱眙渡淮北去，閔列兵南岸，軍士喏聲相聞。

translations.literal: When the Jin crossed north from Xuyi, Min arrayed troops on the south bank; soldiers' shouts of assent could be heard from one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin crossed back north from Xuyi, Min lined his men on the south bank while they shouted their approval across the ranks.

sentences.zh: 金人笑之曰：「寄聲成太尉，有勤護送。」

translations.literal: The Jin laughed and said: "Send word to Grand Marshal Cheng—thanks for the diligent escort."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin laughed and called out, "Tell Grand Marshal Cheng we appreciate the escort."

sentences.zh: 時虜氣已奪，日虞王師之至，委棄戈甲、粟米山積，諸軍多仰以給。

translations.literal: By then the barbarians' spirit was already broken; day by day they feared the imperial army's arrival; they abandoned weapons and armor and grain piled like mountains, and many armies relied on these supplies.
translations.idiomatic: By then the enemy's morale was broken; they feared the Song army daily and abandoned mountains of weapons and grain, which many Song units lived on.

sentences.zh: 惟閔軍多浙人，素不食粟，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Only Min's army had many men from Zhe who were unused to eating grain, and very many died.
translations.idiomatic: Min's men, mostly from Zhejiang and unused to grain rations, suffered heavy deaths.

sentences.zh: 閔至泗州，奏已克復淮東。

translations.literal: When Min reached Sizhou he memorialized that Huaidong had been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou he reported that Huaidong had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 尋入朝，，凡侍從、卿監、閣門、內侍，皆有賂遺。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered court; to every attendant, minister, gate officer, and palace eunuch he gave bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he came to court and bribed every attendant, minister, gate officer, and palace eunuch he met.

sentences.zh: 左正言劉度劾之，猶超拜太尉，主管殿前司公事。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrator Liu Du impeached him, yet he was still promoted over rank to Grand Marshal and put in charge of Palace Command affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrator Liu Du impeached him, yet he was still promoted to Grand Marshal and put in charge of the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 尋復為御史論列，罷太尉，婺州居住，奪慶遠節。

translations.literal: Before long censors again denounced him; he was dismissed as Grand Marshal, ordered to reside at Wuzhou, and stripped of his Qingyuan commission.
translations.idiomatic: Censors soon attacked him again; he was stripped of the Grand Marshal title, ordered to live at Wuzhou, and lost his Qingyuan commission.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，聽自便，歸湖州；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao he was permitted to go where he wished and returned to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiandao era he was allowed to go where he wished and returned to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋詔復節，都統鎮江諸軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict restored his commission and made him overall commander of the armies at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict restored his commission and made him overall commander at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，請詞，致仕，治園第於平江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he requested leave, retired from office, and built an estate at Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he asked to retire, left office, and built an estate at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi he died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1174 at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 子十一人。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons.

sentences.zh: 趙密字微叔，太原清源人。

translations.literal: Zhao Mi, style name Weishu, was a native of Qingyuan in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mi, whose style name was Weishu, came from Qingyuan in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，用材武試崇政殿，授河北隊將，戍燕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe he passed the talent-and-martial examination at the Chongzheng Hall, was appointed squad leader in Hebei, and garrisoned Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114 he passed the talent-and-martial examination at the Chongzheng Hall, was made a squad leader in Hebei, and garrisoned Yan.

sentences.zh: 高宗以大元帥開府，檄統先鋒援京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong opened his Grand Marshal headquarters, he was ordered by dispatch to command the vanguard in relieving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong opened his Grand Marshal headquarters, Mi was ordered to lead the vanguard to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，從張俊討任城寇李昱，俊輕騎先行，遇伏，密奔射斃數人，乃脫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he followed Zhang Jun in suppressing the Rencheng bandit Li Yu; Jun rode ahead lightly, met an ambush; Mi galloped and shot several dead before escaping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1127 he followed Zhang Jun against the Rencheng bandit Li Yu; when Jun rode ahead and was ambushed, Mi galloped forward, shot several men dead, and got him out.

sentences.zh: 擢閣門祗候。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat Gate.

sentences.zh: 俊置靖勝軍，以密統之。

translations.literal: Jun established the Jingsheng Army and put Mi in command of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun formed the Jingsheng Army and put Mi in command.

sentences.zh: 平賊董青、越萬、徐明等，累功轉武節郎、左軍統領。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandits Dong Qing, Yue Wan, Xu Ming, and others; through accumulated merit he was transferred to Martial Festival Gentleman and Commander of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the bandits Dong Qing, Yue Wan, Xu Ming, and others, and through repeated merit rose to Martial Festival Gentleman and commander of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 金兵陷揚州，士民隨乘輿渡江，眾數萬，密露立水濱，麾舟濟之。

translations.literal: When Jin troops took Yangzhou, officials and people followed the imperial carriage across the river—tens of thousands; Mi stood exposed on the bank and directed boats to ferry them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin took Yangzhou, tens of thousands of people followed the emperor across the river; Mi stood on the bank and directed boats to ferry them across.

sentences.zh: 苗傅之變，破赤心軍于臨平。

translations.literal: In the Miao Fu mutiny he defeated the Red Heart Army at Linping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Miao Fu mutiny he defeated the Red Heart Army at Linping.

sentences.zh: 金人犯明州，俊遣密及楊沂中與殊死戰，敗之，進武功大夫，升統制。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked Mingzhou, Jun sent Mi and Yang Yizhong to fight to the death, defeated them, and Mi was advanced to Grand Master of Martial Achievement and promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Mingzhou, Jun sent Mi and Yang Yizhong to fight a desperate battle, routed them, and Mi was promoted to Grand Master of Martial Achievement and made a commander.

sentences.zh: 明年，敵分兵犯滁、濠，密進擊之，且命張守忠以五百騎出全椒縣，伏篁竹間，敵疑，宵遁。

translations.literal: The next year the enemy divided forces to attack Chu and Hao; Mi advanced to strike them and also ordered Zhang Shouzhong with five hundred horsemen out from Quanjiao County to lie in ambush among bamboo groves; the enemy grew suspicious and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the enemy attacked Chu and Hao; Mi struck back and sent Zhang Shouzhong with five hundred horsemen to ambush them in bamboo groves near Quanjiao; the enemy grew suspicious and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 密乃引兵出六丈河，斷其歸路，又敗之。

translations.literal: Mi then led troops out at the Liuzhang River, cut off their retreat, and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Mi then marched to the Liuzhang River, cut off their retreat, and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 進中衛、協忠大夫，和州團練、防禦使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of the Central Guard and Loyal Associate, Militia Training Commissioner and Defender of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Central Guard and Loyal Associate, and made Militia Training Commissioner and Defender of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋拜宣州觀察使，為龍、神衛四廂都指揮使，主管侍衛步軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Observer of Xuanzhou, made Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies, and put in charge of the Palace Foot Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Observer of Xuanzhou, commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard Armies, and put in charge of the palace foot guards.

sentences.zh: 海寇朱明暴橫，密授張守忠方略曰：「海與陸異，窮之則日月相持，非策之善，要在拊定之耳。」

translations.literal: The sea bandit Zhu Ming was violent and overbearing; Mi gave Zhang Shouzhong a plan, saying: "Sea and land differ; driving him to extremity means a protracted stalemate—not a good strategy; the key is to soothe and settle him."
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Zhu Ming was running wild; Mi told Zhang Shouzhong, "Fighting pirates at sea is not like fighting on land; cornering him only prolongs the struggle—the best policy is to win him over peacefully."

sentences.zh: 守忠用其計，明降。

translations.literal: Shouzhong used his plan and Zhu Ming surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong followed his advice and Zhu Ming surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進定江軍承宣使、崇信軍節度使，以年勞轉太尉，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Commissioner of the Dingjiang Army and Military Commissioner of the Chongxin Army; for years of service he was transferred to Grand Marshal and appointed Grand Preceptor with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Dingjiang Army and Military Commissioner of the Chongxin Army, and for long service was made Grand Marshal and Grand Preceptor with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 明年，領殿前都指揮使，獻本軍酒方十六所，積錢十萬緡、銀五萬兩助軍用，詔獎之。

translations.literal: The next year he headed the Palace Army Command, presented sixteen wine recipes of his command, and accumulated one hundred thousand strings and fifty thousand taels of silver to aid military expenses; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took command of the palace armies, presented sixteen wine recipes from his command, and contributed one hundred thousand strings and fifty thousand taels of silver for military expenses; the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 上疏告老，以萬壽觀使奉朝請。

translations.literal: He memorialized to report old age and was made Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and was made Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey with court attendance.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，進少保致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing he was advanced to Junior Guardian and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In 1164 he was promoted to Junior Guardian and retired.

sentences.zh: 俄報金復犯淮，詔密再為殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: Shortly reports came that the Jin again invaded the Huai; Mi was ordered once more to be Commander of the Palace Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the Jin had invaded the Huai again, and Mi was ordered back as commander of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 初，敵聲言航海，朝論選從官視舟師，徹禁旅防守，密不為動，迄如所料。

translations.literal: At first the enemy spread word of a sea expedition; court opinion chose attendant officials to inspect the fleet and withdrew imperial guards from defense; Mi did not stir, and events proved as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: At first the enemy claimed they would attack by sea; the court sent officials to inspect the fleet and pulled palace guards from defense, but Mi did not move—and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 和議成，罷為醴泉使。

translations.literal: When peace was made he was dismissed and made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made he was relieved and made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年九月，致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qiandao he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1165 he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈少傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 劉子羽

translations.literal: Liu Ziyu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyu

sentences.zh: 劉子羽，字彥修，建之崇安人，資政殿學士韐之長子也。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyu, style name Yanxiu, was a native of Chong'an in Jian, eldest son of Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyu, whose style name was Yanxiu, came from Chong'an in Jian and was the eldest son of Academician Liu Ge.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，韐帥浙東，子羽以主管機宜文字佐其父。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe Ge commanded eastern Zhe; Ziyu served his father as director of military planning documents.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xuanhe era Liu Ge commanded eastern Zhejiang, and Ziyu served as his father's planning officer.

sentences.zh: 破睦賊，入主太府、太僕簿，遷衛尉丞。

translations.literal: He defeated the Mu bandits, entered service in the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Court of the Imperial Stud, and was transferred to Assistant Master of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Mu rebels he entered the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Court of the Imperial Stud and was promoted to Assistant Master of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 韐守真定，子羽辟從。

translations.literal: When Ge defended Zhending, Ziyu joined his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge defended Zhending, Ziyu joined his staff.

sentences.zh: 會金人入，父子相誓死守，金人不能拔而去，由是知名。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered, father and son swore to die defending the city; the Jin could not take it and withdrew; thereby he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked, father and son swore to hold the city to the death; the Jin could not take it and withdrew, and Ziyu won fame.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 京城不守，韐死之，既免喪，除秘閣修撰、知池州。

translations.literal: When the capital could not be held Ge died in its defense; after mourning ended Ziyu was appointed Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and Prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Liu Ge died defending it; after mourning Ziyu was made Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and Prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 以書抵宰相，論天下兵勢，當以秦、隴為根本。

translations.literal: By letter he reached the chief minister, arguing that the empire's military situation should take Qin and Long as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the chief minister arguing that the empire's military strategy should rest on Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 改集英殿修撰、知秦州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Compiler of the Hall for Gathering Excellence and Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Compiler of the Hall for Gathering Excellence and Prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，召赴行在，除樞密院檢詳文字。

translations.literal: Before he set out he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Examiner of Documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was summoned to the mobile court and made Examiner of Documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，大將范瓊擁強兵江西，召之弗來，來又不肯釋兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan the great general Fan Qiong held strong troops in Jiangxi; summoned he would not come, and when he came he would not release his army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129 the great general Fan Qiong held a strong army in Jiangxi; when summoned he would not come, and when he did come he refused to disband his troops.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事張浚，與子羽密謀誅之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Jun secretly plotted with Ziyu to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhang Jun secretly plotted with Ziyu to kill him.

sentences.zh: 一日，命張俊以千兵渡江，若備他盜者，使皆甲而來。

translations.literal: One day he ordered Zhang Jun with a thousand troops to cross the river as if guarding against other bandits, and had them all come in armor.
translations.idiomatic: One day he ordered Zhang Jun to cross the river with a thousand men as if guarding against bandits, all in armor.

sentences.zh: 因召俊、瓊及劉光世赴都堂議事，為設飲食，食已，諸公相顧未發。

translations.literal: He then summoned Jun, Qiong, and Liu Guangshi to the chief council hall to discuss affairs, set out food and drink, and after they had eaten the gentlemen looked at one another without acting.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Jun, Qiong, and Liu Guangshi to the chief council hall, served a meal, and after they had eaten the men looked at one another without moving.

sentences.zh: 子羽坐廡下，恐瓊覺，取黃紙趨前，舉以麾瓊曰：「下，有敕，將軍可詣大理置對。」

translations.literal: Ziyu sat in the side hall, fearing Qiong would notice; he took yellow paper and hurried forward, raising it to command Qiong: "Down! There is an edict—the general may go to the Court of Judicial Review to answer charges."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu sat in the side hall, fearing Qiong would notice; he seized a yellow edict, rushed forward, and waved it at Qiong, saying, "Down! By imperial order the general is to answer charges at the Court of Judicial Review."

sentences.zh: 瓊愕不知所為，子羽顧左右擁置輿中，衛以俊兵，送獄。

translations.literal: Qiong was stunned and did not know what to do; Ziyu looked to attendants to seize him and place him in a litter, guarded by Jun's troops, and sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was stunned; Ziyu had attendants seize him, place him in a litter guarded by Jun's troops, and send him to prison.

sentences.zh: 光世出撫其眾，數瓊在圍城中附金人迫二帝出狩狀。

translations.literal: Guangshi went out to reassure Qiong's troops, recounting how in the besieged city Qiong had sided with the Jin and forced the two emperors on the imperial hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi went out to calm Qiong's troops, recounting how Qiong had sided with the Jin during the siege and forced the two emperors into captivity.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「所誅止瓊爾，汝等固天子自將之兵也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Only Qiong is to be executed; you are after all troops personally led by the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Only Qiong is to die; you are still the emperor's own troops."

sentences.zh: 眾皆投刃曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The multitude all cast down their blades and said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The men cast down their weapons and answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 有旨分隸禦營五軍，頃刻而定。

translations.literal: An order came to assign them to the five armies of the Imperial Camp, and in a moment all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: An order came to assign them to the five armies of the Imperial Camp, and within moments all was settled.

sentences.zh: 瓊竟伏誅。

translations.literal: Qiong was ultimately executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 浚以此奇其材。

translations.literal: Jun for this reason marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun marveled at his talent for this.

sentences.zh: 浚宣撫川、陝，辟子羽參議軍事。

translations.literal: When Jun was Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi he recruited Ziyu as military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun became Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi he took Ziyu as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 至秦州，立幕府，節度五路諸將，規以五年而後出師。

translations.literal: Reaching Qinzhou he established a headquarters, directed the generals of the five circuits, and planned to campaign only after five years.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzhou he set up headquarters, directed the generals of five circuits, and planned not to campaign for five years.

sentences.zh: 明年，除徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Awaiting Draftsman of the Huixian Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Awaiting Draftsman of the Huixian Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 金人窺江、淮急，浚念禁衛寡弱，計所以分撓其兵勢者，遂合五路之兵以進。

translations.literal: The Jin were pressing urgently on the Yangtze and Huai; Jun, mindful that the imperial guards were few and weak, devised how to divide and harass their military strength, and therefore united the armies of the five circuits to advance.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin pressed the Yangtze and Huai, Jun, knowing the palace guards were weak, decided to divide the enemy's strength by advancing with all five circuits' armies.

sentences.zh: 子羽以非本計，爭之。

translations.literal: Ziyu held that this was not the original plan and argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu argued that this was not the original plan.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「吾寧不知此？

translations.literal: Jun said: "Do I not know this myself?
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Do you think I do not know that?

sentences.zh: 顧今東南之事方急，不得不為是耳。」

translations.literal: But affairs in the southeast are urgent just now—I cannot but do this."
translations.idiomatic: But the southeast is in crisis now, and I have no choice."

sentences.zh: 遂北至富平，與金人遇，戰不利。

translations.literal: They therefore marched north to Fuping, met the Jin, and the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: They marched north to Fuping, met the Jin, and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 金人乘勝而前，宣撫司退保興州，人情大震。

translations.literal: The Jin pressed their victory forward; the Pacification headquarters withdrew to defend Xingzhou, and popular sentiment was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed their victory; the pacification headquarters fell back to Xingzhou, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 官屬有建策徙治夔州者，子羽叱之曰：「孺子可斬也！

translations.literal: Among the staff some proposed moving the administration to Kuizhou; Ziyu shouted at them: "Such a child deserves beheading!
translations.idiomatic: Some staff proposed moving headquarters to Kuizhou; Ziyu shouted, "That fool deserves death!

sentences.zh: 四川全盛，敵欲入寇久矣，直以川口有鐵山、棧道之險，未敢遽窺耳。

translations.literal: Sichuan is in full strength; the enemy has long wished to invade, but only because the river mouth has the perils of Iron Mountain and the plank roads have they not dared to peer in hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan is still strong; the enemy has long wanted to invade, but the Iron Mountain and plank roads at the river mouth have kept them from daring to enter.

sentences.zh: 今不堅守，縱使深入，而吾僻處夔、峽，遂與關中聲援不相聞，進退失計，悔將何及。

translations.literal: If we do not hold firm now, even if we let them penetrate deep, yet we would sit remote in Kuai and the Gorges, and then with Guanzhong our mutual support would no longer be heard; advance and retreat would lose their plan—what regret could there be afterward?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not hold firm and withdraw to Kuizhou and the gorges, we cut ourselves off from Guanzhong; advance and retreat would be impossible, and regret would come too late.

sentences.zh: 今幸敵方肆掠，未逼近郡。

translations.literal: Now fortunately the enemy are still plundering wildly and have not yet pressed close to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the enemy are still raiding widely and have not yet reached our prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣司但當留駐興州，外系關中之望，內安全蜀之心；

translations.literal: The Pacification headquarters should only remain stationed at Xingzhou, outwardly binding the hopes of Guanzhong, inwardly securing the hearts of Shu;
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters should stay at Xingzhou, keeping hope alive in Guanzhong and reassuring Shu;

sentences.zh: 急遣官屬出關，呼召諸將，收集散亡，分佈險隘，堅壁固壘，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: urgently send staff out of the passes, summon the generals, gather the scattered and lost, deploy them at perilous barriers, strengthen walls and fortify camps, and watch for openings before acting.
translations.idiomatic: urgently send officers beyond the passes to summon the generals, gather the scattered troops, hold the defiles, strengthen the walls, and wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 庶幾猶或可以補前愆而贖後咎，奈何乃為此言乎？」

translations.literal: Perhaps we may still repair former faults and redeem later blame—how can you speak such words?"
translations.idiomatic: We may still repair our earlier mistake—how can you speak of retreat?"

sentences.zh: 浚然子羽言，而諸參佐無敢行者。

translations.literal: Jun approved Ziyu's words, yet none of the advisers dared to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed with Ziyu, but none of the other advisers dared to go.

sentences.zh: 子羽即自請奉命北出，復以單騎至秦州，召諸亡將。

translations.literal: Ziyu at once volunteered to go north on orders, again riding alone to Qinzhou to summon the scattered generals.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu volunteered to go north himself, rode alone to Qinzhou, and summoned the scattered generals.

sentences.zh: 諸亡將聞命大喜，悉以其眾來會。

translations.literal: The scattered generals, hearing the order, were greatly pleased and all brought their forces to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: The scattered generals were overjoyed and all brought their troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 子羽命吳玠柵和尚原，守大散關，而分兵悉守諸險塞。

translations.literal: Ziyu ordered Wu Jie to fortify Heshang Plain and guard Dasanguan, while dividing troops to hold all perilous passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu ordered Wu Jie to fortify Heshang Plain and hold Dasanguan, while posting troops at every defile.

sentences.zh: 金人知有備，引去。

translations.literal: The Jin, knowing there was preparation, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the defenses ready, the Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，金人復聚兵來攻，再為玠所敗。

translations.literal: The next year the Jin again gathered troops to attack and were again defeated by Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jin attacked again and were defeated once more by Wu Jie.

sentences.zh: 浚移治閬州，子羽請獨留河池，調護諸將，以通內外聲援，浚許之。

translations.literal: Jun moved his administration to Langzhou; Ziyu asked to remain alone at Hechi to coordinate the generals and maintain inner and outer mutual support; Jun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun moved to Langzhou; Ziyu asked to stay at Hechi to coordinate the generals and keep communications open, and Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，玠以秦鳳經略使戍河池，王彥以金、均、房鎮撫使戍金州。

translations.literal: The next year Jie as Commissioner for Qin and Feng garrisoned Hechi; Wang Yan as Pacification Commissioner for Jin, Jun, and Fang garrisoned Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wu Jie garrisoned Hechi as Commissioner for Qin and Feng, and Wang Yan garrisoned Jinzhou as Pacification Commissioner for Jin, Jun, and Fang.

sentences.zh: 二鎮皆饑，興元帥臣閉糴，二鎮病之。

translations.literal: Both garrisons suffered famine; the Xingyuan commander closed grain sales, and both garrisons resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Both garrisons were starving; the Xingyuan commander stopped selling grain, and both posts suffered.

sentences.zh: 玠、彥皆願得子羽守漢中，浚乃承制拜子羽利州路經略使兼知興元府。

translations.literal: Jie and Yan both wished to have Ziyu defend Hanzhong; Jun therefore by provisional appointment made Ziyu Commissioner for Lizhou Circuit and concurrently Prefect of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Yan both wanted Ziyu to hold Hanzhong; Jun therefore appointed him Commissioner for Lizhou Circuit and Prefect of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 子羽至漢中，通商輸粟，二鎮遂安。

translations.literal: Ziyu reached Hanzhong, opened trade and transported grain; the two garrisons were then secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyu reached Hanzhong, he restored trade and grain supply; the two garrisons were relieved.

sentences.zh: 除寶文閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Scholar of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Scholar of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金人犯金州。

translations.literal: That winter, the Jurchens invaded Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin attacked Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，王彥失守，退保石泉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Wang Yan lost his defense and withdrew to hold Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Wang Yan's position fell and he withdrew to Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 子羽亟移兵守饒風嶺，馳告玠。

translations.literal: Ziyu urgently moved troops to defend Raofeng Ridge and sent a courier to inform Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu hastily shifted his forces to hold Raofeng Ridge and dispatched a messenger to alert Jie.

sentences.zh: 玠大驚，即越境而東，日夜馳三百里至饒風，列營拒守。

translations.literal: Jie was greatly alarmed; he immediately crossed the border eastward and, driving day and night three hundred li, reached Raofeng, where he arrayed camps to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was shocked and immediately crossed into the next prefecture, riding three hundred li day and night to reach Raofeng, where he made camp to hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 金人悉力仰攻，死傷山積，更募死士，由間道自祖溪關入，繞出玠後。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked uphill with all their strength; the dead and wounded piled like hills. They then recruited death-defying soldiers, entered by a hidden route through Zuxi Pass, and looped around behind Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed the assault uphill at full strength, and casualties piled like hills. They then raised a suicide squad, slipped through Zuxi Pass by a back trail, and got behind Jie.

sentences.zh: 玠遽邀子羽去，子羽不可，而留玠同守定軍山，玠難之，遂西。

translations.literal: Jie suddenly urged Ziyu to leave; Ziyu would not agree and kept Jie to defend Dingjun Mountain together; Jie found this difficult and then went west.
translations.idiomatic: Jie urgently pressed Ziyu to retreat, but Ziyu refused and kept him to hold Dingjun Mountain together. Jie balked and eventually withdrew west.

sentences.zh: 子羽焚興元，退守三泉縣，從兵不滿三百，與士卒取草牙、木甲食之，遺玠書訣別。

translations.literal: Ziyu burned Xingyuan and withdrew to defend Sanquan County; his followers numbered fewer than three hundred. With his soldiers he ate grass sprouts and tree bark for food, and sent Jie a letter of final parting.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu burned Xingyuan and fell back to Sanquan County with fewer than three hundred men. Soldiers and commander alike ate young shoots and bark. He sent Jie a farewell letter.

sentences.zh: 玠時在仙人關，其愛將楊政大呼軍門曰：「節使不可負劉待制，不然，政輩亦舍節使去矣。」

translations.literal: Jie was then at Xianren Pass; his favorite general Yang Zheng shouted at the army gate: "The commissioner must not abandon Assistant Hanlin Academician Liu—otherwise, we too will abandon the commissioner and leave."
translations.idiomatic: Jie was at Xianren Pass when his favored officer Yang Zheng shouted at the gate: "Commissioner, you must not abandon Vice Hanlin Academician Liu—or we will abandon you as well."

sentences.zh: 玠乃間道會子羽，子羽留玠共守三泉。

translations.literal: Jie then went by a hidden route to join Ziyu; Ziyu kept Jie to defend Sanquan together.
translations.idiomatic: Jie took a back trail to rejoin Ziyu, who kept him to hold Sanquan together.

sentences.zh: 玠曰：「關外蜀之門戶，不可輕棄。」

translations.literal: Jie said: "Outside the passes is Shu's gateway; it must not be lightly abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "The territory beyond the passes is the gateway to Shu—it cannot be cast away lightly."

sentences.zh: 復往守仙人關。

translations.literal: He again went to defend Xianren Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to hold Xianren Pass.

sentences.zh: 子羽以潭毒山形鬥拔，其上寬平有水，乃築壁壘，十六日而成。

translations.literal: Ziyu considered Tandu Mountain steep and lofty; its summit was broad, level, and had water, so he built ramparts and fortifications, completing them in sixteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu chose Tandu Mountain, whose peak rose sheer yet offered level ground and water; there he built fortifications in sixteen days.

sentences.zh: 金人已至，距營十數里。

translations.literal: The Jurchens had already arrived, ten-odd li from the camp.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were already close, little more than ten li from the camp.

sentences.zh: 子羽據胡床，坐於壘口。

translations.literal: Ziyu leaned on a folding chair and sat at the mouth of the rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu took a folding chair and sat at the rampart gate.

sentences.zh: 諸將泣告曰：「此非待制坐處。」

translations.literal: The generals wept and reported: "This is not a place for the Assistant Hanlin Academician to sit."
translations.idiomatic: The officers wept and pleaded: "This is no place for you to sit, Vice Hanlin Academician."

sentences.zh: 子羽曰：「子羽今日死於此。」

translations.literal: Ziyu said: "Ziyu will die here today."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said, "I will die here today."

sentences.zh: 敵尋亦引去。

translations.literal: The enemy soon withdrew as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自金人入梁、洋，四蜀復大震。

translations.literal: From the time the Jurchens entered Liang and Yang, the Four Shu were again greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Jin entered Liang and Yang prefectures, all of Sichuan was shaken anew.

sentences.zh: 張浚欲移潼川，子羽遺浚書，言己在此，金人必不南，浚乃止。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun wished to move to Tongchuan; Ziyu sent Jun a letter saying that with himself here the Jurchens would certainly not go south, and Jun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun wanted to shift headquarters to Tongchuan, but Ziyu wrote assuring him that with himself holding the line the Jin would not push south; Jun abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 撒離曷由斜穀北去，子羽謀邀之于武休，不及，既回鳳翔，遣十人持書旗招子羽，子羽盡斬之，而留其一，縱之還，曰：「為我語賊，欲來即來，吾有死爾，何可招也！」

translations.literal: Sa Lihe went north through Xiegu; Ziyu planned to intercept him at Wuxiu but did not reach him in time. After returning to Fengxiang, he sent ten men bearing letters and banners to summon Ziyu; Ziyu executed them all but kept one, released him to return, and said: "Tell the bandits for me: if you wish to come, then come—I have death to offer; how can you summon me!"
translations.idiomatic: Sa Lihe marched north through Xiegu Valley. Ziyu planned an ambush at Wuxiu but arrived too late. Back in Fengxiang, the Jin sent ten envoys with letters and banners to win Ziyu over. He beheaded nine and sent the tenth back with a message: "Tell your masters: come if you like—I am ready to die. Do you imagine I can be bought?"

sentences.zh: 先是，子羽預徙梁、洋公私之積，至是，金人深入，饋不繼，又腹背為子羽、玠所攻，死傷十五六，疫癘且作，亟遁去。

translations.literal: Earlier Ziyu had in advance moved the public and private stores of Liang and Yang; at this point the Jurchens had penetrated deeply, supplies did not follow, and they were attacked front and rear by Ziyu and Jie—fifteen or sixteen tenths were killed or wounded, pestilence was breaking out, and they hastily fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu had already emptied Liang and Yang of stored grain. Now deep in enemy country, the Jin ran out of supplies, caught attacks from front and rear by Ziyu and Jie, and lost perhaps half their force to battle and disease. They fled in haste.

sentences.zh: 子羽出師掩擊，墮溪澗死者不可勝計，餘兵不能自拔者，悉降。

translations.literal: Ziyu sent troops out in a surprise attack; those who fell into streams and ravines and died could not be counted; the remaining troops who could not extricate themselves all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu struck from ambush. Countless Jin drowned in streams and gullies; the rest who could not escape surrendered.

sentences.zh: 始，金人攻蜀，所選士卒千取百，百取十；

translations.literal: At the outset, when the Jurchens attacked Shu, of the soldiers selected, one in a thousand was taken, of a hundred one in ten was taken;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first invaded Shu, they picked their troops with brutal selectivity—one man from every thousand, then one from every hundred—

sentences.zh: 戰被重鎧，登山攻險，每一人前，輒二人推其後，前者死，後者被其甲以進，又死，則又代之，其為必取計如此。

translations.literal: In battle they wore heavy armor; climbing mountains and attacking perilous ground, for each man who went forward, two men always pushed from behind. When the front man died, the man behind donned his armor and advanced; when he died too, another replaced him—such was their plan to take it at all costs.
translations.idiomatic: They marched in heavy mail up steep ground, two men shoving each forward fighter from behind. When one fell, the next pulled on his armor and stepped into his place—and when that man fell, another took his turn. That was how determined they were to win.

sentences.zh: 浚雖衄師，卒全蜀，子羽之力居多。

translations.literal: Although Jun's army was repulsed, he ultimately preserved Shu whole, and Ziyu's contribution was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had lost the field battle, yet Shu held—and Ziyu deserved most of the credit.

sentences.zh: 子羽還興元。

translations.literal: Ziyu returned to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu returned to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐富平之役，與浚俱罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of the Fuping campaign, he was dismissed together with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year both he and Jun were cashiered for the defeat at Fuping.

sentences.zh: 尋為言者所論，責授單州團練副使，白州安置。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by memorialists, demoted to Assistant Military Training Commissioner of Shan Prefecture, and assigned to reside at Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists soon attacked him; he was reduced to Assistant Military Training Commissioner of Shan and ordered to live in exile at Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新除川、陝宣撫副使吳玠，始為裨將，未知名。

translations.literal: Wu Jie, newly appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner for Chuan and Shan, had begun as a staff general and was not yet known by name.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie, newly named Vice Pacification Commissioner for Chuan and Shan, had been an obscure staff officer.

sentences.zh: 子羽獨奇之，言於浚，浚與語大悅，使盡護諸將。

translations.literal: Ziyu alone marked him out as extraordinary, spoke of him to Jun; Jun conversed with him and was greatly pleased, and had him put in charge of all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ziyu saw his promise and recommended him to Zhang Jun, who was delighted in conversation and put him over all the generals.

sentences.zh: 至是，上疏論子羽之功，請納節贖其罪。

translations.literal: At this time he submitted a memorial on Ziyu's merits and asked to surrender his command tally to redeem Ziyu's offense.
translations.idiomatic: Now he memorialized the court praising Ziyu's service and offering to give up his own command seal to clear Ziyu's name.

sentences.zh: 詔聽子羽自便。

translations.literal: An edict permitted Ziyu to do as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The throne allowed Ziyu to go where he chose.

sentences.zh: 明年，復元官，提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: The next year his original office was restored; he was made Superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his rank was restored and he was appointed superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張浚還朝，議合兵大舉，乃請召子羽，令諭旨西帥，以集英殿修撰知鄂州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun returned to court, discussed combining armies for a great offensive, and then requested that Ziyu be summoned to convey the imperial intent to the western commanders; Ziyu was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and Prefect of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, Zhang Jun planned a joint offensive and had Ziyu recalled to carry the emperor's instructions to the western generals; Ziyu was made Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，權都督府參議軍事，與主管機宜文字熊彥詩同撫諭川、陝。

translations.literal: Before long he was Acting Councillor on Military Affairs for the Chief Commandery and, together with Bearer of Secretariat Documents for Military Affairs Xiong Yanshi, jointly pacified and instructed Chuan and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served provisionally as military councillor to the chief commandery and toured Chuan and Shan with Secretariat officer Xiong Yanshi to reassure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 時吳玠屢言軍前乏糧，故令子羽見玠諭指，且與都轉運使趙開計事，並察邊備虛實以聞，時五年冬也。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Jie repeatedly reported that the front lacked grain; therefore Ziyu was sent to meet Jie and convey the imperial instructions, and also to consult with Commissioner-General of Transport Zhao Kai on affairs, and to inspect the border defenses' strengths and weaknesses to report—this was in the winter of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie kept reporting shortages at the front, so Ziyu was sent to explain the court's intent to him, consult with transport commissioner Zhao Kai, and report on border readiness. It was winter of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，與彥詩同還朝。

translations.literal: The next autumn he returned to court together with Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he returned to court with Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 子羽言：「金人未可圖，宜益兵屯田，以俟機會。」

translations.literal: Ziyu said: "The Jurchens cannot yet be targeted; troops should be increased and garrison farming undertaken to await the opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu advised, "The Jin are not ripe for attack. Reinforce the frontier and open garrison farms until the moment comes."

sentences.zh: 時張浚以淮西安撫使劉光世驕惰不肅，密奏請罷之，而以其兵屬子羽。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun, because Huai'an Pacification Commissioner Liu Guangshi was arrogant, lazy, and undisciplined, secretly memorialized requesting his dismissal and that his troops be placed under Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had secretly asked to remove the Huai'an pacification commissioner Liu Guangshi for arrogance and slack discipline, and to put his troops under Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 子羽辭，乃以徽猷閣待制知泉州。

translations.literal: Ziyu declined; he was then made Awaiting Orders at the Huiyao Pavilion and Prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu refused; he was instead made Huiyao Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting and prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，淮西酈瓊叛，張浚罷相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Li Qiong of Huai West rebelled, and Zhang Jun was dismissed as chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Li Qiong rebelled in Huai West and Zhang Jun lost the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 八年，御史常同論子羽十罪，上批出「白州安置」。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Censor Chang Tong charged Ziyu with ten crimes; the emperor's marginal note ordered "assigned to reside at Ba Prefecture."
