translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Censor Chang Tong listed ten crimes against Ziyu; the emperor's endorsement sent him back to exile at Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎曰：「章疏中論及結吳玠事，今方倚玠，恐不自安。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said: "The memorial discusses Ziyu's bond with Wu Jie; the court now relies on Jie—he may grow uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding warned, "The memorial brings up Ziyu's ties to Wu Jie; if the court is depending on Jie now, this may unsettle him."

sentences.zh: 同疏再上，以散官安置漳州。

translations.literal: Chang Tong's memorial was submitted again; Ziyu was assigned to reside at Zhang Prefecture as a dismissed official.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Tong memorialized again, and Ziyu was exiled to Zhang Prefecture as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，樞密使張浚薦子羽復元官，知鎮江府兼沿江安撫使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Grand Councilor Zhang Jun recommended restoring Ziyu's original office; he became Prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture and concurrently Riverine Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Zhang Jun, as chief of military affairs, had Ziyu's rank restored and made him prefect of Zhenjiang and riverine pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 金人入寇，子羽建議清野，淮東之人，皆徙鎮江，撫以恩信，雖兵民雜居，無敢相侵者。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded, Ziyu proposed scorched-earth tactics; the people east of the Huai all moved to Zhenjiang. He comforted them with benevolence and trust, and although soldiers and civilians lived mixed together, none dared to molest one another.
translations.idiomatic: During a Jin invasion Ziyu ordered the countryside cleared; refugees from east of the Huai flooded into Zhenjiang. He ruled with fairness and trust, and even with troops and civilians crowded together there was no disorder.

sentences.zh: 既而金人不至，浚問子羽，子羽曰：「異時金人入寇，飄忽如風雨，今久遲回，必有他意。」

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens did not come; Jun asked Ziyu, and Ziyu said: "In the past when the Jurchens invaded, they were swift as wind and rain; now they linger long—there must be some other intention."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin failed to appear, Zhang Jun asked Ziyu's reading. Ziyu said, "Past raids came like a storm; this long delay means something else."

sentences.zh: 蓋金人以柘皋之敗，欲急和也。

translations.literal: This was because the Jurchens, after their defeat at Zhegao, wished urgently to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, beaten at Zhegao, were eager to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，果遣使議和。

translations.literal: Before long they indeed sent envoys to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys for peace soon followed.

sentences.zh: 復徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: He was again made Awaiting Orders at the Huiyao Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His post as Huiyao Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting was restored.

sentences.zh: 秦檜風諫官論罷之，復提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Qin Hui prompted the remonstrance officials to impeach and dismiss him; he was again made Superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui steered censors to attack him and strip his office; he returned to overseeing the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子珙，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Gong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎朱松以子熹托子羽，子羽與弟子翬篤教之，異時卒為大儒雲。

translations.literal: Zhu Song, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, entrusted his son Xi to Ziyu; Ziyu and his nephew Yu taught him devotedly, and in time he ultimately became a great Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Song of the Ministry of Personnel placed his son Xi in Ziyu's care. Ziyu and his nephew Yu educated him with great devotion, and he later became one of the age's great scholars—Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 呂祉，字安老，建州建陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Anlao, was a native of Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, styled Anlao, was from Jianyang in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，上舍釋褐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuanhe era he received office upon graduation from the Upper Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xuanhe reign he entered service as a graduate of the Upper Academy.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，為右正言，以論事忤執政，通判明州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he became Right Remonstrator; because his policy remonstrances offended those in power, he was made Vice Prefect of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan's second year he served as Right Remonstrator until his blunt memorials angered the ministers and he was posted as vice prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，盜起湖南、北，為荊湖提刑。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing bandits rose in north and south Hunan; he became Judicial Commissioner for Jing and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing's first year, with banditry spreading across Hunan, he was made judicial commissioner for Jing and Hu.

sentences.zh: 祉既至，招捕有方，逾年盜平。

translations.literal: Once Zhi arrived, his methods of recruitment and suppression were effective; within a year the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi pacified the region within a year through shrewd offers and crackdowns.

sentences.zh: 進直秘閣，尋召赴行在。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Access to the Secretariat; soon he was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Secretariat access, he was soon called to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 淮南宣撫使韓世忠將出師，辟祉議軍事，除直徽猷閣，充參議官，辭不行。

translations.literal: Huainan Pacification Commissioner Han Shizhong was about to take the field; he recruited Zhi to consult on military affairs, appointing him Direct Access to the Huiyao Pavilion and filling the post of Councillor, but Zhi declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong, pacification commissioner of Huainan, wanted Lu Zhi as military adviser and offered him a Huiyao post, but Lu declined to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，升直龍圖閣、知建康府。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall and made Prefect of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Dragon Diagram Hall access and prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 祉到官，與通判府事吳若、安撫司準備差遣陳充共議，作《東南防守利便》三卷上之，大略謂：「立國于東南者，當聯絡淮甸、荊、蜀之勢，今臨安僻在海隅，移蹕江上，然後可以系南北離散之心。」

translations.literal: When Zhi took office, together with Vice Prefect for Prefectural Affairs Wu Ruo and Prepared Dispatch Officer of the Pacification Commission Chen Chong he jointly discussed and composed three fascicles of "Advantages in Defending the Southeast," which they submitted. The general purport was: "One who founds a state in the southeast should link the momentum of the Huai region, Jing, and Shu. Now Lin'an sits remote at the sea's edge; only by moving the imperial carriage to the Yangzi can one bind together the scattered hearts of north and south."
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Lu Zhi worked with vice prefect Wu Ruo and pacification staff officer Chen Chong on a three-scroll memorial, "Advantages in Defending the Southeast." Its argument: a southeastern dynasty must knit together the Huai, the middle Yangzi, and Sichuan. Lin'an was too far coastal; moving the court to the Yangzi was the way to hold north and south together.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，金人攻淮，江左戒嚴，獨韓世忠統銳卒在高郵。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year the Jurchens attacked the Huai; the left bank of the Yangzi went on alert; Han Shizhong alone commanded elite troops at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin struck the Huai line; the south bank of the Yangzi mobilized, while Han Shizhong alone held Gaoyou with picked troops.

sentences.zh: 金既陷漣水，破山陽、盱眙，遂犯承州。

translations.literal: Once the Jurchens had taken Lianshui and broken through Shanyang and Xuyi, they then invaded Cheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Lianshui and overrunning Shanyang and Xuyi, they pressed on to Cheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祉上章言：「宜遣兵為世忠援。」

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "Troops should be sent to aid Shizhong."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi memorialized that reinforcements must be sent to Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 既而援兵不至，世忠退保鎮江。

translations.literal: Before long reinforcements did not arrive; Shizhong withdrew to hold Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: No help came; Han Shizhong fell back on Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 祉再上言：「置江北於度外，非命帥宣撫兩淮之意，且恐失中原心。

translations.literal: Zhi again remonstrated: "Treating the north of the Yangzi as outside one's calculations is not the intent of appointing commanders to pacify the Two Huai, and moreover will likely lose the hearts of the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi protested again: "Writing off the north bank betrays the purpose of appointing Huai commanders—and will lose the hearts of patriots in the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 唯當急遣諸將，且乞親禦六師，庶幾上下協心，可以不戰而勝。」

translations.literal: One should urgently dispatch the generals and also beg that the emperor personally lead the Six Armies—in that way perhaps upper and lower will act in concert and victory may be won without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch every general at once, and let Your Majesty lead the armies in person—only then will the realm stand as one and victory come without a fight."

sentences.zh: 於是降詔親征。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict descended ordering the emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 車駕至平江，金人退師。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Pingjiang; the Jurchens withdrew their army.
translations.idiomatic: The court reached Pingjiang and the Jin pulled back.

sentences.zh: 五年，召為中書門下省檢正諸房文字，尋除兵部侍郎兼戶部侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned as Corrector of Documents for All Bureaus of the Secretariat and Chancellery; soon he was appointed Vice Minister of War concurrently Vice Minister of Revenue and Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered the Secretariat as a document corrector, then became vice minister of war and revenue and a reviewing censor.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷刑部侍郎、都督府參議軍事，俄遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Councillor on Military Affairs for the Chief Commandery; shortly he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he moved to vice minister of justice and military councillor at the chief commandery, then quickly to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 劉豫分道入寇，時車駕駐平江，或請回臨安，且令守江防海。

translations.literal: Liu Yu attacked by several routes; the imperial carriage was then stationed at Pingjiang. Some requested returning to Lin'an and ordering defense of the river and protection of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's forces invaded on several axes while the court sat at Pingjiang. Some urged retreat to Lin'an and a policy of river-and-sea defense only.

sentences.zh: 祉獨抗言：「士氣當振，賊鋒可挫，不可遽退以示弱。」

translations.literal: Zhi alone spoke in opposition: "Morale should be roused; the bandit spearhead can be broken—one must not hastily retreat and show weakness."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi alone stood firm: "Raise the army's spirit, break the enemy's thrust—do not retreat and show fear."

sentences.zh: 劉麟眾十萬，已次濠、壽。

translations.literal: Liu Lin's host of one hundred thousand had already encamped at Hao and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin's hundred-thousand-man army was already at Hao and Shou.

sentences.zh: 劉光世在合肥，欲移屯太平州，軍已行，乃命祉馳往軍前，督其還。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi was at Hefei and wished to move his encampment to Taiping Prefecture; the army had already marched, and Zhi was ordered to ride to the front of the army and supervise its return.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi at Hefei tried to relocate to Taipingzhou; his men were already marching when Lu Zhi was sent at full speed to turn them back.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷兵部尚書，升督府參謀軍事，往淮西撫諭諸軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Minister of War and elevated to Staff Councillor on Military Affairs for the Chief Commandery, and went to Huai West to pacify and instruct the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became minister of war and chief military strategist, touring Huai West to steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 浚以劉光世持不戰之論，罷之，乃命行營左護軍前統制王德為都統制，又以統制官酈瓊為之副。

translations.literal: Jun, because Liu Guangshi held the view of not fighting, dismissed him, and then ordered Wang De, former commander of the Left Protective Army of the Field Headquarters, as Overall Commander, and further appointed Control Officer Li Qiong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun removed Liu Guangshi for preaching avoidance of battle, made Wang De overall commander of the former Left Protective Army, and named Li Qiong his deputy.

sentences.zh: 瓊與德素不協，祉還朝，瓊與德交訟于都督府及御史台，乃命德還建康，以其軍隸督府。

translations.literal: Qiong and De had long been incompatible; when Zhi returned to court, Qiong and De mutually sued each other before the Chief Commandery and the Censorate; De was then ordered back to Jiankang and his army placed under the Chief Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong and Wang De were old rivals. After Lu Zhi returned to court they filed rival suits at headquarters and the Censorate. Wang De was recalled to Jiankang and his command placed directly under headquarters.

sentences.zh: 八月，復命祉往廬州節制之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhi was again ordered to go to Lu Prefecture to take command and regulate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lu Zhi was sent back to Luzhou to take command.

sentences.zh: 祉至廬州，瓊等復訟德。

translations.literal: When Zhi reached Lu Prefecture, Qiong and others again sued De.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou, Li Qiong again dragged Wang De into court.

sentences.zh: 祉諭之曰：「若以君等為是，則大相誑。

translations.literal: Zhi instructed them saying: "If I sided with you gentlemen on this, I would be greatly deceiving others.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi told them, "If I ruled for you, I would be telling the grossest lie.

sentences.zh: 然張丞相但喜人向前，儻能立功，雖有大過亦闊略，況此小嫌乎？

translations.literal: Yet Counselor Zhang only delights in men who press forward; if one can achieve merit, even great faults are overlooked—how much more so this small grudge?
translations.idiomatic: But Chancellor Zhang rewards men who fight. Win him glory and even grave faults are forgiven—what is this petty feud?

sentences.zh: 當力為諸公辨之，保無他慮。」

translations.literal: I shall exert myself to plead on your behalf for all of you, guaranteeing no other concerns."
translations.idiomatic: I will speak up for you and see you safe."

sentences.zh: 瓊等感泣。

translations.literal: Qiong and the others were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong and his officers wept with relief.

sentences.zh: 事小定，祉乃密奏乞罷瓊及統制官靳賽兵權。

translations.literal: Once matters had settled slightly, Zhi then secretly memorialized requesting the dismissal of Qiong and Control Officer Jin Sai from their military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When things calmed, Lu Zhi secretly asked the throne to strip Li Qiong and officer Jin Sai of command.

sentences.zh: 其書吏漏語於瓊，瓊令人遮祉所遣郵置，盡得祉所言，大怨怒。

translations.literal: A clerk in his office leaked word to Qiong; Qiong had men intercept the courier post Zhi had dispatched, obtained everything Zhi had said, and was greatly resentful and enraged.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk betrayed the secret. Li Qiong intercepted Lu Zhi's dispatch rider, learned everything, and burned with rage.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷命張俊為淮西宣撫使，置司盱眙；

translations.literal: It happened that the court appointed Zhang Jun Huai West Pacification Commissioner, with headquarters at Xuyi;
translations.idiomatic: About then the court named Zhang Jun Huai West pacification commissioner at Xuyi;

sentences.zh: 楊存中為淮西制置使，劉錡為副，置司廬州；

translations.literal: Yang Cunzhong was made Huai West Military Commissioner, with Liu Yi as deputy, headquarters at Lu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cunzhong Huai West military commissioner at Luzhou with Liu Yi as deputy;

sentences.zh: 召瓊赴行在。

translations.literal: Qiong was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Qiong was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 瓊懼，遂叛。

translations.literal: Qiong was afraid and then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Qiong rebelled.

sentences.zh: 諸將晨謁祉，坐定，瓊袖出文書，示中軍統制官張璟曰：「諸兵官有何罪，張統制乃以如許事聞之朝廷邪？」

translations.literal: In the morning the generals paid court to Zhi; once seated, Qiong produced documents from his sleeve and showed Central Army Control Officer Zhang Jing, saying: "What crime have the military officers committed, that Control Officer Zhang reported such matters to the court?"
translations.idiomatic: At the morning levee Lu Zhi sat with his generals when Li Qiong drew out papers and showed them to central commander Zhang Jing. "What crime did your officers commit," he demanded, "that Zhang reported us to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 祉見之大驚，欲返走，不及，為瓊所執。

translations.literal: When Zhi saw this he was greatly alarmed; he wished to turn and flee but could not in time, and was seized by Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi started up in horror and tried to flee, but Li Qiong seized him.

sentences.zh: 璟及兵馬鈐轄喬仲福，統制劉永、衡友死之。

translations.literal: Jing and Military Horse Commission Director Qiao Zhongfu, and Control Officers Liu Yong and Heng You died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing, horse commission director Qiao Zhongfu, and officers Liu Yong and Heng You were killed.

sentences.zh: 瓊遂率全軍四萬人渡淮降劉豫，擁祉次三塔，距淮三十里。

translations.literal: Qiong then led the entire army of forty thousand men across the Huai to surrender to Liu Yu, escorting Zhi to camp at Santa, thirty li from the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong crossed the Huai with forty thousand men to join Liu Yu, dragging Lu Zhi along to a camp at Santa, thirty li from the river.

sentences.zh: 祉下馬曰：「劉豫逆臣，我豈可見之？」

translations.literal: Zhi dismounted and said: "Liu Yu is a treacherous minister—how could I meet him?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi dismounted. "Liu Yu is a traitor—I will not go before him."

sentences.zh: 眾逼祉上馬，祉罵曰：「死則死於此！」

translations.literal: The crowd pressed Zhi to mount; Zhi cursed, saying: "If I die, I die here!"
translations.idiomatic: They forced him back on his horse. Lu Zhi cursed them: "If I must die, I die here!"

sentences.zh: 又語其眾曰：「劉豫逆臣，爾軍中豈無英雄，乃隨酈瓊去乎？」

translations.literal: He also said to the troops: "Liu Yu is a rebellious minister—are there no heroes in your ranks that you follow Li Qiong?"
translations.idiomatic: He also told the troops, "Liu Yu is a traitor—surely there are heroes among you who will not follow Li Qiong?"

sentences.zh: 眾頗感動，凡千餘人環立不行。

translations.literal: The crowd was quite moved; more than a thousand men stood in a ring and would not move.
translations.idiomatic: The men were deeply moved; more than a thousand stood in a circle and refused to march.

sentences.zh: 瓊恐搖動眾心，急策馬先渡，祉遇害。

translations.literal: Qiong, fearing to shake the troops' hearts, spurred his horse across first; Zhi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would lose the men, Qiong spurred his horse across the river first; Lu Zhi was murdered.

sentences.zh: 時有得祉括發之帛歸吳中者，其妻吳氏持帛自縊以徇葬，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: At that time someone who had obtained cloth from Zhi's bound hair returned to Wu; his wife Lady Wu took the cloth and hanged herself to accompany his burial—hearers mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who recovered cloth from Zhi's bound hair brought it to Wu; his wife Lady Wu hanged herself with it to join his burial, and all who heard mourned her.

sentences.zh: 慶元間，詔立廟賜額，以旌其忠雲。

translations.literal: Between Qingyuan, an edict established a temple and granted an honorific plaque to commend his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingyuan era the court established a temple and granted an honorific plaque in recognition of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 胡世將

translations.literal: Hu Shijiang
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shijiang

sentences.zh: 胡世將，字承公，常州晉陵人，宿之曾孫。

translations.literal: Hu Shijiang, style name Chenggong, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou, great-grandson of Su.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shijiang, whose style name was Chenggong, came from Jinling in Changzhou and was the great-grandson of Hu Su.

sentences.zh: 登崇甯五年進士第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1106 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 範汝為寇閩，以世將為監察御史、福建路撫諭使。

translations.literal: When Fan Ruwei raided Min, Shijiang was made Investigating Censor and Pacification Commissioner for Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ruwei raided Fujian, Shijiang was made Investigating Censor and Pacification Commissioner for Fujian.

sentences.zh: 入境，韓世忠已平賊。

translations.literal: Upon entering the circuit, Han Shizhong had already pacified the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Han Shizhong had already pacified the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右司員外郎，又遷起居郎，遷中書舍人，賜三品服，兼修政局。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Division Outer Section Director of the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted to Master of Documents, then Drafting Middle Secretary, granted third-rank robes, and concurrently revised government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of Revenue, became Master of Documents, then Drafting Middle Secretary, was granted third-rank robes, and helped revise government affairs.

sentences.zh: 坐言者落職奉祠。

translations.literal: Because of critics he was dismissed to temple service.
translations.idiomatic: Critics brought him down and he was sent to temple service.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除徽猷閣待制、知鎮江府，入為禮部侍郎，改刑部，出知洪州，兼江西安撫、制置使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Awaiting Draftsman of the Huixian Pavilion and Prefect of Zhenjiang, entered as Vice Minister of Rites, changed to Punishments, and went out as Prefect of Hongzhou with concurrent Jiangxi Pacification and Reorganization Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Awaiting Draftsman of the Huixian Pavilion and Prefect of Zhenjiang, then Vice Minister of Rites, then Punishments, and finally Prefect of Hongzhou with concurrent Jiangxi pacification and reorganization duties.

sentences.zh: 屬建昌兵變，殺守卒，嬰城以叛，世將以便宜發兵討平之。

translations.literal: When soldiers at Jianchang mutinied, killed the guards, and walled the city in rebellion, Shijiang at discretion sent troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianchang soldiers mutinied, killed the guards, and walled the city in revolt, he sent troops at his discretion and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 除兵部侍郎，復知鎮江。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War and again made Prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of War and again Prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為給事中兼侍講，直學士院，復遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Supervising Censor and Lecturer, entered the Academy, and again promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Supervising Censor and lecturer, entered the Academy, and was again promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋以樞密直學士出為四川安撫制置使，兼知成都府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he went out as Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Sichuan Pacification and Reorganization Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out as Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Sichuan Pacification and Reorganization Commissioner, and Prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 宣撫吳玠以軍無糧，奏請踵至。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie memorialized repeatedly that the army lacked grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie repeatedly reported that his army lacked grain.

sentences.zh: 世將既被命入境，約玠會議。

translations.literal: Once Shijiang received his commission and entered the circuit, he arranged to meet Jie for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: After taking office he arranged to meet Wu Jie for consultation.

sentences.zh: 蜀之餉運，溯嘉陵江千餘里，半年始達。

translations.literal: Shu supplies were transported up the Jialing River for more than a thousand li, taking half a year to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan supplies traveled up the Jialing River for more than a thousand li and took half a year to arrive.

sentences.zh: 於是奏用轉般摺運之法，軍儲稍充，公私便之。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized to use the transfer-and-fold transport method; military stores were gradually filled and public and private affairs were eased.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a transfer-and-fold transport system; military stores gradually filled and both government and people benefited.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，玠卒，以世將為寶文閣學士、宣撫川、陝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, when Jie died, Shijiang was made Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1139, when Wu Jie died, Shijiang was made Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時關陝初復，朝廷分軍移屯熙、秦、鄜延諸道。

translations.literal: At that time Guan and Shaanxi had just been recovered; the court divided the army and shifted garrisons to Xi, Qin, Fuyan, and other routes.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Shaanxi had just been recovered; the court divided the army among garrisons at Xi, Qin, Fuyan, and other routes.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，金人陷同州，入長安，諸路皆震。

translations.literal: The next summer the Jin took Tongzhou and entered Chang'an; every route was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer the Jin took Tongzhou and entered Chang'an, shaking every command.

sentences.zh: 蜀兵既分，聲援幾絕，乃遣大將吳璘、田晟出鳳翔，郭浩出奉天，楊政由赤穀歸河池。

translations.literal: Shu troops were already divided and mutual support nearly cut off; he therefore sent the great generals Wu Lin and Tian Sheng out from Fengxiang, Guo Hao out from Fengtian, and Yang Zheng back from Chigu to Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: With Shu forces divided and support nearly cut off, he sent Wu Lin and Tian Sheng out from Fengxiang, Guo Hao from Fengtian, and Yang Zheng from Chigu back to Hechi.

sentences.zh: 不數日，璘捷於石壁及扶風，金人逡巡不敢度隴，分屯之軍得全師而還。

translations.literal: Within days Lin won victories at Shibi and Fufeng; the Jin hesitated and dared not cross Long, and the divided garrisons returned with their forces intact.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Wu Lin won at Shibi and Fufeng; the Jin hesitated to cross Long, and the scattered garrisons returned intact.

sentences.zh: 詔除端明殿學士。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，朝廷復用兵。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eleventh year the court again took up arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1141 the court resumed hostilities.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，命起復。

translations.literal: He was in mourning for his mother but ordered recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was mourning his mother but was ordered to return to duty.

sentences.zh: 遂復隴州，破岐下諸屯，又取華、虢，兵威稍振。

translations.literal: They then recovered Longzhou, broke the enemy camps below Qi, and also took Hua and Guo; military prestige gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Longzhou, broke enemy camps below Qi, and took Hua and Guo; morale gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瘍發於首。

translations.literal: Before long an ulcer broke out on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an ulcer broke out on his head.

sentences.zh: 除資政殿學士致仕，恩數視簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and retired; his favors equaled those of a Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and retired with honors equal to a Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，命有司給葬事。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-eight; the court ordered the relevant offices to provide funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight; the court ordered officials to provide his funeral.

sentences.zh: 鄭剛中

translations.literal: Zheng Gangzhong
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Gangzhong

sentences.zh: 鄭剛中，字亨仲，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Zheng Gangzhong, style name Hengzhong, was a native of Jinhua in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Gangzhong, whose style name was Hengzhong, came from Jinhua in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士甲科，累官為監察御史，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the top class and through successive offices became Investigating Censor and was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the top class, rose through the ranks to Investigating Censor, and was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 剛中由秦檜薦於朝，檜主和議，剛中不敢言。

translations.literal: Gangzhong was recommended to court by Qin Gui; Gui advocated peace, and Gangzhong did not dare speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong was recommended by Qin Gui; Gui pushed peace, and Gangzhong did not dare object.

sentences.zh: 移宗正少卿，請去，不許，改秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, requested leave, was not permitted, and was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, asked to leave, was refused, and was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 金歸侵疆，檜遣剛中為宣諭司參謀官；

translations.literal: When the Jin returned the invaded territory, Gui sent Gangzhong as staff officer of the Pacification Commission;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin returned invaded territory, Gui sent Gangzhong as staff officer of the Pacification Commission;

sentences.zh: 及還，除禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: on his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: on his return he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 復遣剛中為川、陝宣諭使，諭諸將罷兵，尋充陝西分畫地界使。

translations.literal: Gangzhong was again sent as Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi to instruct the generals to cease fighting, and soon was also made Boundary Demarcation Commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent as Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi to order the generals to stand down, and soon became Boundary Demarcation Commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 金使烏陵贊謨入境，欲盡取階、成、岷、鳳、秦、商六州，剛中力爭不從；

translations.literal: The Jin envoy Wulingsanmo entered the border wishing to take entirely the six prefectures of Jie, Cheng, Min, Feng, Qin, and Shang; Gangzhong argued strenuously and would not yield;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy Wulingsanmo demanded all six prefectures of Jie, Cheng, Min, Feng, Qin, and Shang; Gangzhong refused;

sentences.zh: 又欲姑取商、秦，于大散關立界，剛中又堅不從。

translations.literal: they then wished temporarily to take Shang and Qin and set the boundary at Dasanguan; Gangzhong again firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: they then asked for Shang and Qin with the boundary at Dasanguan; Gangzhong refused again.

sentences.zh: 繼除川、陝宣撫副使。

translations.literal: He was next appointed Deputy Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Deputy Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 兀術遣人力求和尚原，剛中恐敗和好，以和尚原自紹興四年後不系吳地分，於是割秦、商之半，棄和尚原以與金。

translations.literal: Wuzhu sent men urgently demanding Heshang Plain; Gangzhong feared breaking the peace, holding that since the fourth year of Shaoxing Heshang Plain had not been Wu territory—therefore he ceded half of Qin and Shang and abandoned Heshang Plain to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu urgently demanded Heshang Plain; fearing to break the peace, Gangzhong claimed it had not been Song territory since 1134, ceded half of Qin and Shang, and gave up Heshang Plain.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命剛中去「陝」字，為四川宣撫副使。

translations.literal: The court ordered Gangzhong to drop the character "Shaan," making him Deputy Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court removed "Shaan" from his title, making him Deputy Pacification Commissioner for Sichuan alone.

sentences.zh: 剛中治蜀，頗有方略。

translations.literal: Gangzhong governed Shu with considerable strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong governed Sichuan with considerable ability.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司舊在綿、閬間，及胡世將代吳玠，就居河池，饋餉不繼。

translations.literal: The pacification headquarters had formerly been between Mian and Lang; when Hu Shijiang replaced Wu Jie he moved to Hechi, and supplies did not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters had been between Mian and Lang; when Hu Shijiang replaced Wu Jie he moved to Hechi and supplies failed.

sentences.zh: 剛中奏：利州在潭毒關內，與興、洋諸關聲援相接，乞移司利州。

translations.literal: Gangzhong memorialized: Lizhou lies within Tandu Pass and connects in mutual support with the passes of Xing and Yang—he begged to move the headquarters to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Lizhou lay within Tandu Pass and connected with the Xing and Yang passes, and asked to move headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 自是省費百萬。

translations.literal: From this more than a million was saved.
translations.idiomatic: This saved more than a million strings.

sentences.zh: 剛中始至，即欲移屯一軍，大將楊政不從，呼政語之曰：「剛中雖書生，不畏死！」

translations.literal: When Gangzhong first arrived he wished to shift one army's camp; the great general Yang Zheng refused; he summoned Zheng and said to him: "Though Gangzhong is a scholar, he does not fear death!"
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he tried to move one army; Yang Zheng refused; he summoned Zheng and said, "I may be a scholar, but I do not fear death!"

sentences.zh: 聲色俱厲，政即聽命。

translations.literal: His voice and expression were both fierce; Zheng at once obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: His voice and manner were fierce; Zheng obeyed at once.

sentences.zh: 都統每入謁，必庭參然後就坐。

translations.literal: Whenever a commander-in-chief came to audience he had to perform courtyard obeisance before being seated.
translations.idiomatic: Every commander-in-chief had to perform courtyard obeisance before sitting down.

sentences.zh: 吳璘升檢校少師來謝，語閽吏，乞講鈞敵之禮。

translations.literal: Wu Lin, promoted Acting Junior Guardian, came to give thanks and told the gate officer he wished to use equal-status courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin, now Acting Junior Guardian, came to give thanks and asked the gate officer for equal-status courtesy.

sentences.zh: 剛中曰：「少師雖尊，猶都統制耳，儻變常禮，是廢軍容。」

translations.literal: Gangzhong said: "Though Junior Guardian is exalted, he is still a commander-in-chief; if we change the regular rite, we destroy military decorum."
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong said, "Junior Guardian is exalted, but he is still a commander; change the rite and you destroy military decorum."

sentences.zh: 行禮如故。

translations.literal: The rites were performed as before.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony proceeded as before.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲四川雜征，又請減成都府路對糴及宣撫司激賞錢。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish miscellaneous levies in Sichuan and also asked to reduce the Chengdu circuit grain-purchase quota and pacification headquarters incentive funds.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished miscellaneous Sichuan levies and cut the Chengdu grain-purchase quota and pacification incentive funds.

sentences.zh: 時剛中于階、成二州營田，抵秦州界，凡三千餘頃，歲收十八萬斛。

translations.literal: At that time Gangzhong ran military farms in Jie and Cheng prefectures reaching the Qinzhou border—more than three thousand qing in all, yielding 180,000 hu annually.
translations.idiomatic: He ran military farms in Jie and Cheng reaching Qinzhou—over three thousand qing yielding 180,000 hu a year.

sentences.zh: 先是，川口屯兵十萬，分隸三大將：吳璘屯興州，楊政屯興元府，郭浩屯金州，皆建帥節；

translations.literal: Previously, 100,000 troops at the river mouth were divided among three great generals: Wu Lin at Xingzhou, Yang Zheng at Xingyuan Prefecture, Guo Hao at Jinzhou—all established command banners;
translations.idiomatic: Previously 100,000 troops at the river mouth were divided among Wu Lin at Xingzhou, Yang Zheng at Xingyuan, and Guo Hao at Jinzhou, each with his own command;

sentences.zh: 而統制官知成州王彥、知階州姚仲、知西和州程俊、知鳳州楊從儀亦領沿邊安撫。

translations.literal: while commanders Wang Yan of Chengzhou, Yao Zhong of Jiezhou, Cheng Jun of Xihezhou, and Yang Congyi of Fengzhou also held frontier pacification posts.
translations.idiomatic: while Wang Yan, Yao Zhong, Cheng Jun, and Yang Congyi also held frontier pacification posts.

sentences.zh: 剛中請分利州為東、西路，以興元府、利閬洋巴劍州、大安軍七郡為東路，治興元，命政為安撫；

translations.literal: Gangzhong asked to divide Lizhou into eastern and western routes: the seven prefectures of Xingyuan, Li, Lang, Yang, Ba, Jian, and Da'an as the eastern route, administered from Xingyuan with Zheng as pacifier;
translations.idiomatic: He divided Lizhou into eastern and western routes: seven eastern prefectures administered from Xingyuan under Yang Zheng;

sentences.zh: 以興、階、成、西和、文、隴、鳳七州為西路，治興州，命璘為安撫；

translations.literal: the seven prefectures of Xing, Jie, Cheng, Xihe, Wen, Long, and Feng as the western route, administered from Xingzhou with Lin as pacifier;
translations.idiomatic: seven western prefectures administered from Xingzhou under Wu Lin;

sentences.zh: 而命浩為金、房、開、達州安撫；

translations.literal: and Hao made pacifier of Jin, Fang, Kai, and Dazhou;
translations.idiomatic: and Guo Hao pacifier of Jin, Fang, Kai, and Da;

sentences.zh: 諸裨將領安撫者皆罷。

translations.literal: all subordinate generals who had held pacification posts were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: all lesser generals holding pacification posts were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 弛夔路酒禁，復利州錢監為紹興監。

translations.literal: He relaxed the wine monopoly on the Kuizhou route and restored the Lizhou mint as the Shaoxing Mint.
translations.idiomatic: He relaxed the Kuizhou wine monopoly and restored the Lizhou mint as the Shaoxing Mint.

sentences.zh: 時軍已罷，移屯內郡，剛中言逐路各有漕司，都漕宜罷。

translations.literal: At that time fighting had ceased and troops moved to inner prefectures; Gangzhong said each route already had transport commissioners and the overall transport post should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting ended and troops moved inland, he said each route already had transport commissioners and the overall post should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 秦檜怒剛中在蜀專擅，令侍御史汪勃奏置四川財賦總領官，以趙不棄為之，不隸宣撫司。

translations.literal: Qin Gui, angered that Gangzhong acted arbitrarily in Shu, had Attendant Censor Wang Bo memorialize to establish an overall Sichuan finance commissioner, with Zhao Buqi appointed to it, not subordinate to the pacification headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Gui, angered by Gangzhong's autonomy in Shu, had Wang Bo establish an overall Sichuan finance commissioner, Zhao Buqi, outside pacification control.

sentences.zh: 不棄牒宣撫司，剛中怒，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Buqi sent documents to the pacification headquarters; Gangzhong was angry, and from this a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Buqi sent orders to the pacification headquarters; Gangzhong was furious and a rift opened.

sentences.zh: 不棄頗求剛中陰事言於檜，檜陽召不棄歸，因召剛中。

translations.literal: Buqi sought out Gangzhong's private faults and reported them to Gui; Gui ostensibly recalled Buqi but thereby summoned Gangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Buqi gathered Gangzhong's secrets for Gui; Gui ostensibly recalled Buqi but summoned Gangzhong.

sentences.zh: 剛中語人曰：「孤危之跡，獨賴上知之耳。」

translations.literal: Gangzhong said to others: "In my isolated peril I rely only on the emperor's understanding."
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong told others, "In my isolation I rely only on the emperor's understanding."

sentences.zh: 檜聞愈怒，遂罷，責桂陽軍居住；

translations.literal: When Gui heard he grew still angrier; Gangzhong was dismissed and ordered to reside at Guiyang Army;
translations.idiomatic: Gui heard and grew angrier; Gangzhong was dismissed and exiled to Guiyang;

sentences.zh: 再責濠州團練副使，復州安置；

translations.literal: again reduced to Assistant Military Training Commissioner of Hao and ordered to live at Fu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: reduced again to Assistant Military Training Commissioner of Hao and sent to Fu Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 再徙封州，卒。

translations.literal: again transferred to Fengzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: then transferred to Fengzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自紹興和議成，材武善謀之士，無所用其力。

translations.literal: The commentary says: After the Shaoxing peace treaty, men of martial talent and good counsel had no place to use their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: After the Shaoxing peace, men of martial talent and strategic counsel had nowhere to use their strength.

sentences.zh: 若王友直之矯制起兵，李寶之立功膠西，成閔、趙密皆足以斬將搴旗，劉子羽轉戰屢勝，呂祉不從劉豫，胡世將、鄭剛中威震巴蜀。

translations.literal: Wang Youzhi forged an edict to raise troops; Li Bao won merit at Jiaoxi; Cheng Min and Zhao Mi were both able to seize banners from the enemy; Liu Ziyu won repeated victories in battle; Lu Zhi would not follow Liu Yu; Hu Shijiang and Zheng Gangzhong awed Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhi forged an edict to raise troops; Li Bao won glory at Jiaoxi; Cheng Min and Zhao Mi could have seized enemy banners; Liu Ziyu won battle after battle; Lu Zhi refused Liu Yu; Hu Shijiang and Zheng Gangzhong awed Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 皆中道以歿，是以知宋不克興復也。

translations.literal: All died midway—thereby one knows Song could not recover the realm.
translations.idiomatic: All died before their time—proof that Song could not restore the empire.
